This policy identifies Azure Cache for Redis instances lacking the redundancy needed to withstand a zone outage.

policies.name: 3d02a511-74e5-4dab-a5fd-878704d4a61a
policies.displayName: [Preview]: Azure Data Factory pipelines should only communicate with allowed domains
policies.description: To prevent data & token exfiltration, set the domains that Azure Data Factory should be allowed to communicate with. Note: While in public preview, the compliance for this policy is not reported, & for policy to be applied to Data Factory, please enable outbound rules functionality in the ADF studio. For more information, visit https://aka.ms/data-exfiltration-policy.

policies.name: 493c215d-2554-5976-bc81-57d2c04fc8c1
policies.displayName: [Preview]: Azure Database for MySQL Flexible Server should be Zone Resilient
policies.description: Azure Database for MySQL Flexible Server can be configured to be either Zone Aligned, Zone Redundant, or neither. MySQL Server that has a standby server selected in same zone for high availability is considered Zone Aligned. In contrast, MySQL Server that has a standby server selected to be in a different zone for high availability is recognized as Zone Redundant. This policy helps identify and enforce these resilience configurations.

policies.name: 493c215d-2553-4976-bc81-57d2c04fc8c1
policies.displayName: [Preview]: Azure Database for PostgreSQL Flexible Server should be Zone Resilient
policies.description: Azure Database for PostgreSQL Flexible Server can be configured to be either Zone Aligned, Zone Redundant, or neither. PostgreSQL Server that has a standby server selected in same zone for high availability is considered Zone Aligned. In contrast, PostgreSQL Server that has a standby server selected to be in a different zone for high availability is recognized as Zone Redundant. This policy helps identify and enforce these resilience configurations.

policies.name: bf45a74c-ed4f-4300-8afe-d6f0abdfe75b
policies.displayName: [Preview]: Azure HDInsight should be Zone Aligned
policies.description: Azure HDInsight can be configured to be Zone Aligned or not. Azure HDInsight that has exactly one entry in its zones array is considered Zone Aligned. This policy ensures that an Azure HDInsight cluster is configured to operate within a single availability zone.

policies.name: 2d7e144b-159c-44fc-95c1-ac3dbf5e6e54
policies.displayName: [Preview]: Azure IoT Hub should use customer-managed key to encrypt data at rest
policies.description: Encryption of data at rest in IoT Hub with customer-managed key adds a second layer of encryption on top of the default service-managed keys, enables customer control of keys, custom rotation policies, and ability to manage access to data through key access control. Customer-managed keys must be configured during creation of IoT Hub. For more information on how to configure customer-managed keys, see https://aka.ms/iotcmk.

policies.name: 1d478a74-21ba-4b9f-9d8f-8e6fced0eec5
policies.displayName: [Preview]: Azure Key Vault Managed HSM keys should have an expiration date
policies.description: To use this policy in preview, you must first follow these instructions at https://aka.ms/mhsmgovernance. Cryptographic keys should have a defined expiration date and not be permanent. Keys that are valid forever provide a potential attacker with more time to compromise the key. It is a recommended security practice to set expiration dates on cryptographic keys.

policies.name: ad27588c-0198-4c84-81ef-08efd0274653
policies.displayName: [Preview]: Azure Key Vault Managed HSM Keys should have more than the specified number of days before expiration
policies.description: To use this policy in preview, you must first follow these instructions at https://aka.ms/mhsmgovernance. If a key is too close to expiration, an organizational delay to rotate the key may result in an outage. Keys should be rotated at a specified number of days prior to expiration to provide sufficient time to react to a failure.

policies.name: e58fd0c1-feac-4d12-92db-0a7e9421f53e
policies.displayName: [Preview]: Azure Key Vault Managed HSM keys using elliptic curve cryptography should have the specified curve names
policies.description: To use this policy in preview, you must first follow these instructions at https://aka.ms/mhsmgovernance. Keys backed by elliptic curve cryptography can have different curve names. Some applications are only compatible with specific elliptic curve keys. Enforce the types of elliptic curve keys that are allowed to be created in your environment.

policies.name: 86810a98-8e91-4a44-8386-ec66d0de5d57
policies.displayName: [Preview]: Azure Key Vault Managed HSM keys using RSA cryptography should have a specified minimum key size
policies.description: To use this policy in preview, you must first follow these instructions at https://aka.ms/mhsmgovernance. Set the minimum allowed key size for use with your key vaults. Use of RSA keys with small key sizes is not a secure practice and doesn't meet many industry certification requirements.

policies.name: 19ea9d63-adee-4431-a95e-1913c6c1c75f
policies.displayName: [Preview]: Azure Key Vault Managed HSM should disable public network access
policies.description: Disable public network access for your Azure Key Vault Managed HSM so that it's not accessible over the public internet. This can reduce data leakage risks. Learn more at: https://docs.microsoft.com/azure/key-vault/managed-hsm/private-link#allow-trusted-services-to-access-managed-hsm.

policies.description: Private link provides a way to connect Azure Key Vault Managed HSM to your Azure resources without sending traffic over the public internet. Private link provides defense in depth protection against data exfiltration. Learn more at: https://docs.microsoft.com/azure/key-vault/managed-hsm/private-link

policies.description: Azure Kubernetes Service Managed Clusters can be configured to be Zone Redundant or not. The policy checks the node pools in the cluster and ensures that avaialbilty zones are set for all the node pools.

Enforcing this policy helps ensure that Backup and Site Recovery is appropriately configured for zone resilience, reducing the risk of downtime during zone outages.

policies.name: 4bd1f3c0-9443-49ad-b8bc-7c17a92b5924

policies.description: Backup Vaults can be configured to be Zone Redundant or not. Geo Redundant or Locally Redundant Backup Vaults are not considered resilient. Enforcing this policy helps ensure that Backup Vaults are appropriately configured for zone resilience, reducing the risk of downtime during zone outages.

You can optionally include Azure Files in storage accounts containing a specified tag to control the scope of assignment.

policies.name: d8659d5a-a3bd-444d-98ea-570bceb568cf

The vault can be in the same or a different subscription. This is useful when a central team manages backups across subscriptions. You can optionally include Azure Files in storage accounts with a specified tag to control the scope of the policy assignment.

Doing this is useful when different application teams in your organization are allocated separate resource groups and need to manage their own backups and restores. You can optionally exclude Azure Files in storage accounts containing a specified tag to control the scope of assignment.

policies.name: e159e079-0ddd-4905-97c9-79a8fca6d880

The vault can be in the same or a different subscription. This is useful when a central team manages backups across subscriptions. You can optionally exclude Azure Files in storage accounts with a specified tag to control the scope of the policy assignment.

policies.description: Private endpoints connect your virtual network to Azure services without a public IP address at the source or destination. By mapping private endpoints to your site recovery resources of Recovery Services vaults, you can reduce data leakage risks. To use private links, managed service identity must be assigned to Recovery Services Vaults. Learn more about private links at: https://docs.microsoft.com/azure/site-recovery/azure-to-azure-how-to-enable-replication-private-endpoints.

policies.description: Configure virtual machines created with Shared Image Gallery images to automatically install the Guest Attestation extension to allow Azure Security Center to proactively attest and monitor the boot integrity. Boot integrity is attested via Remote Attestation.

policies.description: Configure VMSS created with Shared Image Gallery images to automatically install the Guest Attestation extension to allow Azure Security Center to proactively attest and monitor the boot integrity. Boot integrity is attested via Remote Attestation.

policies.displayName: [Preview]: Configure Windows Recovery Environment (WinRE) on Windows machines
policies.description: Creates a Guest Configuration assignment to configure Enables the Windows Recovery Environment (WinRE) on Windows machines.

policies.name: 357cbd2d-b5c0-4c73-b40c-6bd84f06ce09
policies.displayName: [Preview]: Configure Windows Server to disable local users.
policies.description: Creates a Guest Configuration assignment to configure disabling local users on Windows Server. This ensures that Windows Servers can only be accessed by AAD (Azure Active Directory) account or a list of explicitly allowed users by this policy, improving overall security posture.

policies.name: 42daa904-5969-47ef-92fb-b75df946195a
policies.displayName: [Preview]: Container App should be Zone Redundant
policies.description: Container App can be configured to be Zone Redundant or not. A Container App is Zone Redundant if its managed environment's 'ZoneRedundant' property is set to true. This policy identifies Container App lacking the redundancy needed to withstand a zone outage.

policies.name: f58e8c0a-3c79-431a-abf8-cd1b895478e8
policies.displayName: [Preview]: Container Instances should be Zone Aligned
policies.description: Container Instances can be configured to be Zone Aligned or not. They are considered Zone Aligned if they have only one entry in their zones array. This policy ensures that they are configured to operate within a single availability zone.

policies.name: 9d2b0a20-57d6-474c-9d12-44a4a20999c6
policies.displayName: [Preview]: Container Registry should be Zone Redundant
policies.description: Container Registry can be configured to be Zone Redundant or not. When the zoneRedundancy property for a Container Registry is set to 'Disabled', it means the registry is not Zone Redundant. Enforcing this policy helps ensure that your Container Registry is appropriately configured for zone resilience, reducing the risk of downtime during zone outages.

policies.name: c4857be7-912a-4c75-87e6-e30292bcdf78
policies.displayName: [Preview]: Container Registry should use a virtual network service endpoint
policies.description: This policy audits any Container Registry not configured to use a virtual network service endpoint.

policies.name: 44c5a1f9-7ef6-4c38-880c-273e8f7a3c24
policies.displayName: [Preview]: Cosmos Database Accounts should be Zone Redundant
policies.description: Cosmos Database Accounts can be configured to be Zone Redundant or not. If the 'enableMultipleWriteLocations' is set to 'true' then all locations must have a 'isZoneRedundant' property and it must be set to 'true'. If the 'enableMultipleWriteLocations' is set to 'false' then the primary location ('failoverPriority' set to 0) must have a 'isZoneRedundant' property and it must be set to 'true'. Enforcing this policy ensures Cosmos Database Accounts are appropriately configured for zone redundancy.

policies.name: 7148a409-0d59-4baa-925b-b3aae486a14e
policies.displayName: [Preview]: Enable system-assigned identity to SQL VM
policies.description: Enable system-assigned identity at scale to SQL virtual machines. You need to assign this policy at subscription level. Assign at resource group level will not work as expected.

policies.name: ae243d87-5cf3-4dce-90bd-6d62be328de9
policies.displayName: [Preview]: Event Hubs should be Zone Redundant
policies.description: Event Hubs can be configured to be Zone Redundant or not. Event Hubs are Zone Redundant if it's 'zoneRedundant' property is set to 'true'. Enforcing this policy helps ensure that Event Hubs are appropriately configured for zone resilience, reducing the risk of downtime during zone outages.

policies.name: 14b4e776-9fab-44b0-b53f-38d2458ea8be
policies.displayName: [Preview]: Extended Security Updates should be installed on Windows Server 2012 Arc machines.
policies.description: Windows Server 2012 Arc machines should have installed all the Extended Security Updates released by Microsoft. This policy requires that the Guest Configuration prerequisites have been deployed to the policy assignment scope. For details, visit https://aka.ms/gcpol

policies.name: 18314dc7-a25d-420c-a069-f094b25ff91b
policies.displayName: [Preview]: Firewalls should be Zone Resilient
policies.description: Firewalls can be configured to be either Zone Aligned, Zone Redundant, or neither. Firewalls that have exactly one entry in its zones array are considered Zone Aligned. In contrast, Firewalls with 3 or more entries in its zones array are recognized as Zone Redundant. This policy helps identify and enforce these resilience configurations.

policies.displayName: [Preview]: Guest Attestation extension should be installed on supported Linux virtual machines
policies.description: Install Guest Attestation extension on supported Linux virtual machines to allow Azure Security Center to proactively attest and monitor the boot integrity. Once installed, boot integrity will be attested via Remote Attestation. This assessment applies to Trusted Launch and Confidential Linux virtual machines.

policies.displayName: [Preview]: Host and VM networking should be protected on Azure Stack HCI systems
policies.description: Protect data on the Azure Stack HCI hosts network and on virtual machine network connections.

policies.name: bdff5235-9f40-4a32-893f-38a03d5d607c
policies.displayName: [Preview]: Install Azure Backup Extension in AKS clusters (Managed Cluster) with a given tag.
policies.description: Installing the Azure Backup Extension is a pre-requisite for protecting your AKS Clusters. Enforce installation of backup extension on all AKS clusters containing a given tag. Doing this can help you manage Backup of AKS Clusters at scale.

policies.name: 9a021087-bba6-42fd-b535-bba75297566b
policies.displayName: [Preview]: Install Azure Backup Extension in AKS clusters (Managed Cluster) without a given tag.
policies.description: Installing the Azure Backup Extension is a pre-requisite for protecting your AKS Clusters. Enforce installation of backup extension on all AKS clusters without a particular tag value. Doing this can help you manage Backup of AKS Clusters at scale.

policies.name: 47031206-ce96-41f8-861b-6a915f3de284
policies.displayName: [Preview]: IoT Hub device provisioning service data should be encrypted using customer-managed keys (CMK)
policies.description: Use customer-managed keys to manage the encryption at rest of your IoT Hub device provisioning service. The data is automatically encrypted at rest with service-managed keys, but customer-managed keys (CMK) are commonly required to meet regulatory compliance standards. CMKs enable the data to be encrypted with an Azure Key Vault key created and owned by you. Learn more about CMK encryption at https://aka.ms/dps/CMK.

policies.name: 5e5a0673-649e-4d50-bf9d-5a387a4e2081
policies.displayName: [Preview]: Kubernetes cluster containers should use only allowed sysctl interfaces
policies.description: Containers should use only allowed sysctl interfaces in a Kubernetes cluster. This policy is generally available for Kubernetes Service (AKS), and preview for Azure Arc enabled Kubernetes. For more information, see https://aka.ms/kubepolicydoc.

policies.name: d9e8f2c1-4c5a-4f5c-8b5a-2abf1e9f7b4d
policies.displayName: [Preview]: Kubernetes cluster should implement accurate Pod Disruption Budgets
policies.description: Prevents faulty Pod Disruption Budgets, ensuring a minimum number of operational pods. Refer to the official Kubernetes documentation for details. Relies on Gatekeeper data replication and syncs all Deployment, StatefulSet, and PodDisruptionBudget resources scoped to it into OPA. Before applying this policy, ensure that the synced resources won't strain your memory capacity. All resources of these kinds across namespaces will sync. Note: currently in preview for Kubernetes Service (AKS).

policies.name: b81f454c-eebb-4e4f-9dfe-dca060e8a8fd
policies.displayName: [Preview]: Kubernetes clusters should restrict creation of given resource type
policies.description: Given Kubernetes resource type should not be deployed in certain namespace.

policies.name: b89ebd51-73f9-4e3e-a1ac-c1c143aaa500
policies.displayName: [Preview]: Kubernetes clusters should use unique ingress hostnames
policies.description: Ensure Ingress resources have unique hostnames across the cluster. Duplicate ingress hostnames can cause routing conflicts where traffic intended for one service is incorrectly routed to another. This policy syncs Ingress resources into OPA via Gatekeeper. Before applying, verify Gatekeeper pods memory capacity won't be exceeded. Parameters apply to specific namespaces, but it syncs all resources of that type across all namespaces. Currently in preview for Kubernetes Service (AKS).

policies.name: 70aa7a1c-b0c7-4b2f-922b-8489d97cbb9f
policies.displayName: [Preview]: Linux machines should meet requirements for the Azure security baseline for Docker hosts
policies.description: Requires that prerequisites are deployed to the policy assignment scope. For details, visit https://aka.ms/gcpol. The machine is not configured correctly for one of the recommendations in the Azure security baseline for Docker hosts.

policies.name: 63594bb8-43bb-4bf0-bbf8-c67e5c28cb65
policies.displayName: [Preview]: Linux machines should meet STIG compliance requirement for Azure compute
policies.description: Requires that prerequisites are deployed to the policy assignment scope. For details, visit https://aka.ms/gcpol. Machines are non-compliant if the machine is not configured correctly for one of the recommendations in STIG compliance requirement for Azure compute. DISA (Defense Information Systems Agency) provides technical guides STIG (Security Technical Implementation Guide) to secure compute OS as required by Department of Defense (DoD). For more details, https://public.cyber.mil/stigs/.

policies.name: e79ffbda-ff85-465d-ab8e-7e58a557660f
policies.displayName: [Preview]: Linux machines with OMI installed should have version 1.6.8-1 or later
policies.description: Requires that prerequisites are deployed to the policy assignment scope. For details, visit https://aka.ms/gcpol. Due to a security fix included in version 1.6.8-1 of the OMI package for Linux, all machines should be updated to the latest release. Upgrade apps/packages that use OMI to resolve the issue. For more information, see https://aka.ms/omiguidance.

policies.name: 13a6c84f-49a5-410a-b5df-5b880c3fe009
policies.displayName: [Preview]: Linux virtual machines should use only signed and trusted boot components
policies.description: All OS boot components (boot loader, kernel, kernel drivers) must be signed by trusted publishers. Defender for Cloud has identified untrusted OS boot components on one or more of your Linux machines. To protect your machines from potentially malicious components, add them to your allow list or remove the identified components.

policies.name: b1bb3592-47b8-4150-8db0-bfdcc2c8965b
policies.displayName: [Preview]: Linux virtual machines should use Secure Boot
policies.description: To protect against the installation of malware-based rootkits and boot kits, enable Secure Boot on supported Linux virtual machines. Secure Boot ensures that only signed operating systems and drivers will be allowed to run. This assessment only applies to Linux virtual machines that have the Azure Monitor Agent installed.

policies.name: 42daa901-5969-47ef-92cb-b75df946195a
policies.displayName: [Preview]: Load Balancers should be Zone Resilient
policies.description: Load Balancers with a sku other than Basic inherit the resilience of the Public IP addresses in their frontend. When combined with the 'Public IP addresses should be Zone Resilient' policy, this approach ensures the necessary redundancy to withstand a zone outage.

policies.name: d855fd7a-9be5-4d84-8b75-28d41aadc158
policies.displayName: [Preview]: Load tests using Azure Load Testing should be run only against private endpoints from within a virtual network.
policies.description: Azure Load Testing engine instances should use virtual network injection for the following purposes: 1. Isolate Azure Load Testing engines to a virtual network. 2. Enable Azure Load Testing engines to interact with systems in either on premises data centers or Azure service in other virtual networks. 3. Empower customers to control inbound and outbound network communications for Azure Load Testing engines.

policies.name: af99038c-02fd-4a2f-ac24-386b62bf32de
policies.displayName: [Preview]: Machines should have ports closed that might expose attack vectors
policies.description: Azure's Terms Of Use prohibit the use of Azure services in ways that could damage, disable, overburden, or impair any Microsoft server, or the network. The exposed ports identified by this recommendation need to be closed for your continued security. For each identified port, the recommendation also provides an explanation of the potential threat.

policies.name: 344ea7ca-2ba8-4d68-859b-317239714b2c
policies.displayName: [Preview]: Managed Disks should be Zone Resilient
policies.description: Managed Disks can be configured to be either Zone Aligned, Zone Redundant, or neither. Managed Disks with exactly one zone assignment are Zone Aligned. Managed Disks with a sku name that ends in ZRS are Zone Redundant. This policy assists in identifying and enforcing these resilience configurations for Managed Disks.

policies.name: ae62c456-33de-4dc8-b100-7ce9028a7d99
policies.displayName: [Preview]: Managed Identity Federated Credentials from Azure Kubernetes should be from trusted sources
policies.description: This policy limits federeation with Azure Kubernetes clusters to only clusters from approved tenants, approved regions, and a specific exception list of additional clusters.

policies.name: fd1a8e20-2c4f-4a6c-9354-b58d786d9a1f
policies.displayName: [Preview]: Managed Identity Federated Credentials from GitHub should be from trusted repository owners
policies.description: This policy limits federation with GitHub repos to only approved repository owners.

policies.name: 2571b7c3-3056-4a61-b00a-9bc5232234f5
policies.displayName: [Preview]: Managed Identity Federated Credentials should be from allowed issuer types
policies.description: This policy limits whether Managed Identities can use federated credentials, which common issuer types are allowed, and provides a list of allowed issuer exceptions.

policies.name: ece3c79b-2caf-470d-a5f5-66470c4fc649
policies.displayName: [Preview]: Microsoft Dev Box Pools should not use Microsoft Hosted Networks.
policies.description: Disallows the use of Microsoft Hosted Networks when creating Pool resources.

policies.name: 0d6d79a8-8406-4e87-814d-2dcd83b2c355
policies.displayName: [Preview]: Microsoft Managed DevOps Pools should be provided with valid subnet resource in order to configure with own virtual network.
policies.description: Disallows creating Pool resources if a valid subnet resource is not provided.

policies.name: 18314dc7-a25d-420c-a069-f094b25ff919
policies.displayName: [Preview]: NAT gateway should be Zone Aligned
policies.description: NAT gateway can be configured to be Zone Aligned or not. NAT gateway that has exactly one entry in its zones array is considered Zone Aligned. This policy ensures that an NAT gateway is configured to operate within a single availability zone.

policies.name: ec2c1bce-5ad3-4b07-bb4f-e041410cd8db
policies.displayName: [Preview]: Nexus Compute Machines should meet Security Baseline
policies.description: Utilizes the Azure Policy Guest Configuration agent for auditing. This policy ensures that machines adhere to the Nexus compute security baseline, encompassing various recommendations designed to fortify machines against a range of vulnerabilities and unsafe configurations (Linux only).

policies.name: 2fe7ba7d-f670-41f5-8b70-b61dc7dfbe18

Public IP addresses that are regional, with exactly one entry in their zones array are considered Zone Aligned. In contrast, Public IP addresses that are regional, with 3 or more entries in their zones array are recognized as Zone Redundant. This policy helps identify and enforce these resilience configurations.

Public IP prefixes that have exactly one entry in their zones array are considered Zone Aligned. In contrast, Public IP prefixes with 3 or more entries in their zones array are recognized as Zone Redundant. This policy helps identify and enforce these resilience configurations.

policies.name: 11e3da8c-1d68-4392-badd-0ff3c43ab5b0
policies.displayName: [Preview]: Recovery Services vaults should use private link
policies.description: Azure Private Link lets you connect your virtual network to Azure services without a public IP address at the source or destination. The Private Link platform handles the connectivity between the consumer and services over the Azure backbone network. By mapping private endpoints to Azure Recovery Services vaults, data leakage risks are reduced. Learn more about private links for Azure Site Recovery at: https://aka.ms/HybridScenarios-PrivateLink and https://aka.ms/AzureToAzure-PrivateLink.

policies.name: dabf7c7f-5354-42de-a92a-8367f538dd71
policies.displayName: [Preview]: Restrict resource types to Azure services supported in Azure Local disconnected operations

policies.name: 97566dd7-78ae-4997-8b36-1c7bfe0d8121
policies.displayName: [Preview]: Secure Boot should be enabled on supported Windows virtual machines
policies.description: Enable Secure Boot on supported Windows virtual machines to mitigate against malicious and unauthorized changes to the boot chain. Once enabled, only trusted bootloaders, kernel and kernel drivers will be allowed to run. This assessment applies to Trusted Launch and Confidential Windows virtual machines.

policies.name: d3ee5dcf-0c6d-49ab-aee4-f250583a7bdc
policies.displayName: [Preview]: Service Bus should be Zone Redundant
policies.description: Service Bus can be configured to be Zone Redundant or not. When the 'zoneRedundant' property is set to 'false' for a Service Bus, it means it is not configured for Zone Redundancy. This policy identifies and enforces the Zone Redundancy configuration for Service Bus instances.

policies.name: 075896de-f4f8-465b-b6d8-9e73725bb62d
policies.displayName: [Preview]: Service Fabric Clusters should be Zone Redundant
policies.description: Service Fabric Clusters can be configured to be Zone Redundant or not. Servicefabric Clusters whose nodeType do not have the multipleAvailabilityZones set to true are not Zone Redundant. This policy identifies Servicefabric Clusters lacking the redundancy needed to withstand a zone outage.

policies.displayName: [Preview]: Sets Kubernetes cluster container securityContext.runAsUser fields to 1000, a non-root user id
policies.description: Reduces attack surface introduced by escalating privileges as root user in the presence of security vulnerabilities.

policies.displayName: [Preview]: Sets Kubernetes cluster containers' secure computing mode profile type to RuntimeDefault if not present.
policies.description: Setting secure computing mode profile type for containers to prevent unauthorized and potentially harmful system calls to the kernel from user space.

policies.name: 97de439f-fd35-4d43-a693-3644f51a51fd
policies.displayName: [Preview]: Sets Kubernetes cluster init containers securityContext.runAsUser fields to 1000, a non-root user id
policies.description: Reduces attack surface introduced by escalating privileges as root user in the presence of security vulnerabilities.

policies.name: 6bcd4321-fb89-4e3e-bf6c-999c13d47f43
policies.displayName: [Preview]: Sets Kubernetes cluster init containers' secure computing mode profile type to RuntimeDefault if not present.
policies.description: Setting secure computing mode profile type for init containers to prevent unauthorized and potentially harmful system calls to the kernel from user space.

policies.name: fe74a23d-79e4-401c-bd0d-fd7a5b35af32
policies.displayName: [Preview]: Sets Kubernetes cluster Pod securityContext.runAsUser fields to 1000, a non-root user id
policies.description: Reduces attack surface introduced by escalating privileges as root user in the presence of security vulnerabilities.

policies.name: 4ee3ee6a-96ea-4d25-9c00-17f11d2e02c8
policies.displayName: [Preview]: Sets Privilege escalation in the Pod spec in init containers to false.
policies.description: Setting Privilege escalation to false in init containers increases security by preventing containers from allowing privilege escalation such as via set-user-ID or set-group-ID file mode.

policies.name: d77df159-718b-4aca-b94b-8e8890a98231
policies.displayName: [Preview]: Sets Privilege escalation in the Pod spec to false.
policies.description: Setting Privilege escalation to false increases security by preventing containers from allowing privilege escalation such as via set-user-ID or set-group-ID file mode.

policies.name: 5c58d54b-87f0-4dcd-83ea-e855fc988997
policies.displayName: [Preview]: Sets UnhealthyPodEvictionPolicy to 'AlwaysAllow'
policies.description: Sets Pod Disruption Budget's UnhealthyPodEvictionPolicy to 'AlwaysAllow' to allow for evicting even unhealthy pods when performing cluster administration

policies.name: 6221cac0-bb8d-40f4-9535-5d03f713f054
policies.displayName: [Preview]: SQL Databases should be Zone Redundant
policies.description: SQL Databases can be configured to be Zone Redundant or not. Databases with the 'zoneRedundant' setting set to 'false' are not configured for zone redundancy. This policy helps identify SQL databases that need zone redundancy configuration to enhance availability and resilience within Azure.

policies.name: f16a3ca9-b57a-4392-b660-4c1f8442aa8d
policies.displayName: [Preview]: SQL Elastic database pools should be Zone Redundant
policies.description: SQL Elastic database pools can be configured to be Zone Redundant or not. SQL Elastic database pools are Zone Redundant if it's 'zoneRedundant' property is set to 'true'. Enforcing this policy helps ensure that Event Hubs are appropriately configured for zone resilience, reducing the risk of downtime during zone outages.

policies.name: 0fc92280-604b-4f23-9e04-5ef98d1a28df
policies.displayName: [Preview]: SQL Managed Instances should be Zone Redundant
policies.description: SQL Managed Instances can be configured to be Zone Redundant or not. Instances with the 'zoneRedundant' setting set to 'false' are not configured for zone redundancy. This policy helps identify SQL managedInstances that need zone redundancy configuration to enhance availability and resilience within Azure.

policies.name: 85b005b2-95fc-4953-b9cb-f9ee6427c754
policies.displayName: [Preview]: Storage Accounts should be Zone Redundant
policies.description: Storage Accounts can be configured to be Zone Redundant or not. If a Storage Account's SKU name does not end with 'ZRS' or its kind is 'Storage,' it is not Zone Redundant. This policy ensures that your Storage Accounts use ae Zone Redundant configuration.

policies.name: d3903bdf-ab85-4cce-85d3-2934d77629d4
policies.displayName: [Preview]: Virtual Machine Scale Sets should be Zone Resilient
policies.description: Virtual Machine Scale Sets can be configured to be either Zone Aligned, Zone Redundant, or neither. Virtual Machine Scale Sets that have exactly one entry in their zones array are considered Zone Aligned. In contrast, Virtual Machine Scale Sets with 3 or more entries in their zones array and a capacity of at least 3 are recognized as Zone Redundant. This policy helps identify and enforce these resilience configurations.

policies.name: 40d17f6f-a9d2-4f1d-8c37-a699a5372a87
policies.displayName: [Preview]: Virtual Machine Scale Sets with more than 2 availability zones should have automatic AZ rebalancing enabled
policies.description: This policy enables automatic AZ rebalancing for Virtual Machine Scale Sets that are otherwise zone resilient. Automatic zone rebalancing helps to ensure that your Virtual Machine Scale Sets are evenly distributed across the zones in the region.

policies.name: f6358610-e532-4236-b178-4c65865eb262
policies.displayName: [Preview]: Virtual machines guest attestation status should be healthy
policies.description: Guest attestation is performed by sending a trusted log (TCGLog) to an attestation server. The server uses these logs to determine whether boot components are trustworthy. This assessment is intended to detect compromises of the boot chain which might be the result of a bootkit or rootkit infection. This assessment only applies to Trusted Launch enabled virtual machines that have Guest Attestation extension installed.

policies.name: 42f4f3a2-7d20-4c13-a05d-01857a626c22
policies.displayName: [Preview]: Virtual Machines should be Zone Aligned
policies.description: Virtual Machines can be configured to be Zone Aligned or not. They are considered Zone Aligned if they have only one entry in their zones array. This policy ensures that they are configured to operate within a single availability zone.

policies.name: da8a2248-6b4a-44a7-96bf-bf1c0dd208c3
policies.displayName: [Preview]: Virtual network gateways should be Zone Redundant
policies.description: Virtual network gateways can be configured to be Zone Redundant or not. Virtual network gateways whose SKU name or tier does not end with 'AZ' are not Zone Redundant. This policy identifies Virtual network gateways lacking the redundancy needed to withstand a zone outage.

policies.name: 1c30f9cd-b84c-49cc-aa2c-9288447cc3b3
policies.displayName: [Preview]: vTPM should be enabled on supported virtual machines
policies.description: Enable virtual TPM device on supported virtual machines to facilitate Measured Boot and other OS security features that require a TPM. Once enabled, vTPM can be used to attest boot integrity. This assessment only applies to trusted launch enabled virtual machines.

policies.name: 50c52fc9-cb21-4d99-9031-d6a0c613361c
policies.displayName: [Preview]: Windows machines should meet STIG compliance requirements for Azure compute
policies.description: Requires that prerequisites are deployed to the policy assignment scope. For details, visit https://aka.ms/gcpol. Machines are non-compliant if the machine is not configured correctly for one of the recommendations in STIG compliance requirements for Azure compute. DISA (Defense Information Systems Agency) provides technical guides STIG (Security Technical Implementation Guide) to secure compute OS as required by Department of Defense (DoD). For more details, https://public.cyber.mil/stigs/.

policies.name: 50b83b09-03da-41c1-b656-c293c914862b
policies.displayName: A custom IPsec/IKE policy must be applied to all Azure virtual network gateway connections
policies.description: This policy ensures that all Azure virtual network gateway connections use a custom Internet Protocol Security(Ipsec)/Internet Key Exchange(IKE) policy. Supported algorithms and key strengths - https://aka.ms/AA62kb0

policies.name: 4f11b553-d42e-4e3a-89be-32ca364cad4c
policies.displayName: A maximum of 3 owners should be designated for your subscription
policies.description: It is recommended to designate up to 3 subscription owners in order to reduce the potential for breach by a compromised owner.

Azure Security Center's standard pricing tier includes vulnerability scanning for your virtual machines at no extra cost. Additionally, Security Center can automatically deploy this tool for you.

policies.description: Azure Security Center has identified some of your network security groups' inbound rules to be too permissive. Inbound rules should not allow access from 'Any' or 'Internet' ranges. This can potentially enable attackers to target your resources.

policies.name: 8ac833bd-f505-48d5-887e-c993a1d3eea0
policies.displayName: API endpoints in Azure API Management should be authenticated
policies.description: API endpoints published within Azure API Management should enforce authentication to help minimize security risk. Authentication mechanisms are sometimes implemented incorrectly or are missing. This allows attackers to exploit implementation flaws and to access data. Learn More about the OWASP API Threat for Broken User Authentication here: https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/api-management/mitigate-owasp-api-threats#broken-user-authentication

policies.name: c8acafaf-3d23-44d1-9624-978ef0f8652c
policies.displayName: API endpoints that are unused should be disabled and removed from the Azure API Management service
policies.description: As a security best practice, API endpoints that haven't received traffic for 30 days are considered unused and should be removed from the Azure API Management service. Keeping unused API endpoints may pose a security risk to your organization. These may be APIs that should have been deprecated from the Azure API Management service but may have been accidentally left active. Such APIs typically do not receive the most up to date security coverage.

policies.name: ee7495e7-3ba7-40b6-bfee-c29e22cc75d4
policies.displayName: API Management APIs should use only encrypted protocols
policies.description: To ensure security of data in transit, APIs should be available only through encrypted protocols, like HTTPS or WSS. Avoid using unsecured protocols, such as HTTP or WS.

policies.name: c15dcc82-b93c-4dcb-9332-fbf121685b54
policies.displayName: API Management calls to API backends should be authenticated
policies.description: Calls from API Management to backends should use some form of authentication, whether via certificates or credentials. Does not apply to Service Fabric backends.

policies.name: 92bb331d-ac71-416a-8c91-02f2cb734ce4
policies.displayName: API Management calls to API backends should not bypass certificate thumbprint or name validation
policies.description: To improve the API security, API Management should validate the backend server certificate for all API calls. Enable SSL certificate thumbprint and name validation.

policies.name: b741306c-968e-4b67-b916-5675e5c709f4
policies.displayName: API Management direct management endpoint should not be enabled
policies.description: The direct management REST API in Azure API Management bypasses Azure Resource Manager role-based access control, authorization, and throttling mechanisms, thus increasing the vulnerability of your service.

policies.name: d5448c98-e503-4fdd-bcd2-784960c00d04
policies.displayName: API Management policies should inherit parent scope policies using <base />
policies.description: Ensures that every API Management policy includes the <base /> tag at the beginning of each policy section - <inbound>, <outbound>, <backend>, and <on-error> - to inherit policies from parent scopes. Omitting <base /> can lead to bypassing shared rules such as authentication, logging, rate limits, and other critical controls. Learn more: https://aka.ms/apim/policies/how-to

policies.name: f1cc7827-022c-473e-836e-5a51cae0b249
policies.displayName: API Management secret named values should be stored in Azure Key Vault
policies.description: Named values are a collection of name and value pairs in each API Management service. Secret values can be stored either as encrypted text in API Management (custom secrets) or by referencing secrets in Azure Key Vault. To improve security of API Management and secrets, reference secret named values from Azure Key Vault. Azure Key Vault supports granular access management and secret rotation policies.

policies.name: 73ef9241-5d81-4cd4-b483-8443d1730fe5
policies.displayName: API Management service should use a SKU that supports virtual networks
policies.description: With supported SKUs of API Management, deploying service into a virtual network unlocks advanced API Management networking and security features which provides you greater control over your network security configuration. Learn more at: https://aka.ms/apimvnet.

policies.name: ef619a2c-cc4d-4d03-b2ba-8c94a834d85b
policies.displayName: API Management services should use a virtual network
policies.description: Azure Virtual Network deployment provides enhanced security, isolation and allows you to place your API Management service in a non-internet routable network that you control access to. These networks can then be connected to your on-premises networks using various VPN technologies, which enables access to your backend services within the network and/or on-premises. The developer portal and API gateway, can be configured to be accessible either from the Internet or only within the virtual network.

policies.name: df73bd95-24da-4a4f-96b9-4e8b94b402bd
policies.displayName: API Management should disable public network access to the service configuration endpoints
policies.description: To improve the security of API Management services, restrict connectivity to service configuration endpoints, like direct access management API, Git configuration management endpoint, or self-hosted gateways configuration endpoint.

policies.name: ffe25541-3853-4f4e-b71d-064422294b11
policies.displayName: API Management should have username and password authentication disabled
policies.description: To better secure developer portal, username and password authentication in API Management should be disabled. Configure user authentication through Azure AD or Azure AD B2C identity providers and disable the default username and password authentication.

policies.name: 3aa03346-d8c5-4994-a5bc-7652c2a2aef1
policies.displayName: API Management subscriptions should not be scoped to all APIs
policies.description: API Management subscriptions should be scoped to a product or an individual API instead of all APIs, which could result in an excessive data exposure.

policies.name: 3d9f5e4c-9947-4579-9539-2a7695fbc187
policies.displayName: App Configuration should disable public network access
policies.description: Disabling public network access improves security by ensuring that the resource isn't exposed on the public internet. You can limit exposure of your resources by creating private endpoints instead. Learn more at: https://aka.ms/appconfig/private-endpoint.

policies.name: 967a4b4b-2da9-43c1-b7d0-f98d0d74d0b1
policies.displayName: App Configuration should use a customer-managed key
policies.description: Customer-managed keys provide enhanced data protection by allowing you to manage your encryption keys. This is often required to meet compliance requirements.

policies.name: 89c8a434-18f0-402c-8147-630a8dea54e0
policies.displayName: App Configuration should use a SKU that supports private link
policies.description: When using a supported SKU, Azure Private Link lets you connect your virtual network to Azure services without a public IP address at the source or destination. The private link platform handles the connectivity between the consumer and services over the Azure backbone network. By mapping private endpoints to your app configuration instances instead of the entire service, you'll also be protected against data leakage risks. Learn more at: https://aka.ms/appconfig/private-endpoint.

policies.name: d242c24b-bac7-439e-8af7-22d7dcfd3c4f
policies.displayName: App Configuration should use geo-replication
policies.description: Use the geo-replication feature to create replicas in other locations of your current configuration store for enhanced resiliency and availability. Additionally, having multi-region replicas lets you better distribute load, lower latency, protect against datacenter outages, and compartmentalize globally distributed workloads. Learn more at: https://aka.ms/appconfig/geo-replication.

policies.name: ca610c1d-041c-4332-9d88-7ed3094967c7

By mapping private endpoints to your app configuration instances instead of the entire service, you'll also be protected against data leakage risks. Learn more at: https://aka.ms/appconfig/private-endpoint.

policies.name: b08ab3ca-1062-4db3-8803-eec9cae605d6
policies.displayName: App Configuration stores should have local authentication methods disabled
policies.description: Disabling local authentication methods improves security by ensuring that App Configuration stores require Microsoft Entra identities exclusively for authentication. Learn more at: https://go.microsoft.com/fwlink/?linkid=2161954.

policies.name: a83269e2-b4f7-4a3f-b5ed-897c787cbc7c
policies.displayName: App network configuration should deny link to external private endpoints
policies.description: This policy applies exclusively to Mission Platform products and services; usage outside of these scopes is not supported. Deny external private endpoints linked to apps in this tenant.

policies.name: 0e3ccb86-ad68-43a5-8cd0-42035638b199
policies.displayName: App Service app slots should disable public network access.

policies.name: a88d589f-2b09-4b50-8998-9a4e71d7b746
policies.displayName: App Service app slots should disable SSH
policies.description: Azure App Service allows you to open an SSH session to a container running in the service. policies.name: 5747353b-1ca9-42c1-a4dd-b874b894f3d4
policies.displayName: App Service app slots should enable configuration routing to Azure Virtual Network
policies.description: By default, configuration traffic (image pull, content share, backup/restore) is not routed through regional VNET integration. For API < 2024-11-01, set 'vnetImagePullEnabled', 'vnetContentShareEnabled', 'vnetBackupRestoreEnabled' to true. For API >= 2024-11-01, set the corresponding 'outboundVnetRouting' properties or 'outboundVnetRouting.allTraffic' to true. Learn more: https://aka.ms/appservice-vnet-configuration-routing.

policies.displayName: App Service app slots should enable end to end encryption

policies.name: f5c0bfb3-acea-47b1-b477-b0edcdf6edc1

Alternatively, set 'outboundVnetRouting.allTraffic' to route all traffic. Configuration traffic is handled separately by the configuration routing policy.

This policy only applies to Linux apps. This policy requires you to specify a PHP version that meets your requirements.

policies.name: 2d048aca-6479-4923-88f5-e2ac295d9af3
policies.displayName: App Service Environment apps should not be reachable over public internet
policies.description: To ensure apps deployed in an App Service Environment are not accessible over public internet, one should deploy App Service Environment with an IP address in virtual network. To set the IP address to a virtual network IP, the App Service Environment must be deployed with an internal load balancer.

policies.name: b5c4b32e-8699-4bfa-8868-9ed118e9982f
policies.displayName: App Service Environment apps should not be reachable over public internet.
policies.description: This policy applies exclusively to Mission Platform products and services; usage outside of these scopes is not supported. To ensure apps deployed in an App Service Environment are not accessible over public internet, one should deploy App Service Environment with an IP address in virtual network. policies.name: 817dcf37-e83d-4999-a472-644eada2ea1e
policies.displayName: App Service Environment should be configured with strongest TLS Cipher suites
policies.description: The two most minimal and strongest cipher suites required for App Service Environment to function correctly are : TLS_ECDHE_RSA_WITH_AES_256_GCM_SHA384 and TLS_ECDHE_RSA_WITH_AES_128_GCM_SHA256.

policies.name: 50d7880f-06c8-402f-9236-0417e5b1559c
policies.displayName: App Service Environment should have Control and Data Ports bound to ILB
policies.description: This policy applies exclusively to Mission Platform products and services; usage outside of these scopes is not supported. Setting Internal Load Balancing Mode (ilbMode) to 'Web, Publishing' binds HTTP/HTTPS traffic on ports 80/443 and control/data channel ports for FTP to an ILB allocated Virtual Network Address.

policies.name: fb74e86f-d351-4b8d-b034-93da7391c01f
policies.displayName: App Service Environment should have internal encryption enabled
policies.description: Setting InternalEncryption to true encrypts the pagefile, worker disks, and internal network traffic between the front ends and workers in an App Service Environment. To learn more, refer to https://docs.microsoft.com/azure/app-service/environment/app-service-app-service-environment-custom-settings#enable-internal-encryption.

policies.name: bfe08d89-8736-48a7-b88e-76fa3f286881
policies.displayName: App Service Environment should have internal encryption enabled.

policies.name: d6545c6b-dd9d-4265-91e6-0b451e2f1c50
policies.displayName: App Service Environment should have TLS 1.0 and 1.1 disabled
policies.description: TLS 1.0 and 1.1 are out-of-date protocols that do not support modern cryptographic algorithms. Disabling inbound TLS 1.0 and 1.1 traffic helps secure apps in an App Service Environment.

policies.name: a475e840-2781-4c79-aaf0-4047828759b1
policies.displayName: App Service Environments in this tenant should deny link to external private endpoints
policies.description: This policy applies exclusively to Mission Platform products and services; usage outside of these scopes is not supported. Deny external private endpoints linked to App Service Environments in this tenant.

policies.name: 51cf6de4-d195-4172-abd3-ec28ff386558

New 'modify' effect policies are available that support remediation of tags on existing resources (see https://aka.ms/modifydoc).

policies.name: 630c64f9-8b6b-4c64-b511-6544ceff6fd6
policies.displayName: Authentication to Linux machines should require SSH keys
policies.description: Although SSH itself provides an encrypted connection, using passwords with SSH still leaves the VM vulnerable to brute-force attacks. The most secure option for authenticating to an Azure Linux virtual machine over SSH is with a public-private key pair, also known as SSH keys. Learn more: https://docs.microsoft.com/azure/virtual-machines/linux/create-ssh-keys-detailed.

policies.name: dea83a72-443c-4292-83d5-54a2f98749c0
policies.displayName: Automation Account should have Managed Identity
policies.description: Use Managed Identities as the recommended method for authenticating with Azure resources from the runbooks. Managed identity for authentication is more secure and eliminates the management overhead associated with using RunAs Account in your runbook code .

policies.name: 3657f5a0-770e-44a3-b44e-9431ba1e9735
policies.displayName: Automation account variables should be encrypted
policies.description: It is important to enable encryption of Automation account variable assets when storing sensitive data

policies.name: 955a914f-bf86-4f0e-acd5-e0766b0efcb6
policies.displayName: Automation accounts should disable public network access
policies.description: Disabling public network access improves security by ensuring that the resource isn't exposed on the public internet. You can limit exposure of your Automation account resources by creating private endpoints instead. Learn more at: https://docs.microsoft.com/azure/automation/how-to/private-link-security.

policies.name: 3aa87b5a-7813-4b57-8a43-42dd9df5aaa7
policies.displayName: Azure Active Directory Domain Services managed domains should use TLS 1.2 only mode
policies.description: Use TLS 1.2 only mode for your managed domains. By default, Azure AD Domain Services enables the use of ciphers such as NTLM v1 and TLS v1. These ciphers may be required for some legacy applications, but are considered weak and can be disabled if you don't need them. When TLS 1.2 only mode is enabled, any client making a request that is not using TLS 1.2 will fail. Learn more at https://docs.microsoft.com/azure/active-directory-domain-services/secure-your-domain.

policies.name: 2e9411a0-0c5a-44b3-9ddb-ff10a1a2bf28
policies.displayName: Azure Active Directory should use private link to access Azure services
policies.description: Azure Private Link lets you connect your virtual networks to Azure services without a public IP address at the source or destination. The Private Link platform handles the connectivity between the consumer and services over the Azure backbone network. By mapping private endpoints to Azure AD, you can reduce data leakage risks. Learn more at: https://aka.ms/privateLinkforAzureADDocs. It should be only used from isolated VNETs to Azure services, with no access to the Internet or other services (M365).

policies.name: a049bf77-880b-470f-ba6d-9f21c530cf83
policies.displayName: Azure AI Search service should use a SKU that supports private link
policies.description: With supported SKUs of Azure AI Search, Azure Private Link lets you connect your virtual network to Azure services without a public IP address at the source or destination. The private link platform handles the connectivity between the consumer and services over the Azure backbone network. By mapping private endpoints to your Search service, data leakage risks are reduced. Learn more at: https://aka.ms/azure-cognitive-search/inbound-private-endpoints.

policies.name: ee980b6d-0eca-4501-8d54-f6290fd512c3
policies.displayName: Azure AI Search services should disable public network access
policies.description: Disabling public network access improves security by ensuring that your Azure AI Search service is not exposed on the public internet. Creating private endpoints can limit exposure of your Search service. Learn more at: https://aka.ms/azure-cognitive-search/inbound-private-endpoints.

policies.name: 6300012e-e9a4-4649-b41f-a85f5c43be91
policies.displayName: Azure AI Search services should have local authentication methods disabled
policies.description: Disabling local authentication methods improves security by ensuring that Azure AI Search services exclusively require Azure Active Directory identities for authentication. Learn more at: https://aka.ms/azure-cognitive-search/rbac. Note that while the disable local authentication parameter is still in preview, the deny effect for this policy may result in limited Azure AI Search portal functionality since some features of the Portal use the GA API which does not support the parameter.

policies.name: 76a56461-9dc0-40f0-82f5-2453283afa2f
policies.displayName: Azure AI Search services should use customer-managed keys to encrypt data at rest
policies.description: Enabling encryption at rest using a customer-managed key on your Azure AI Search services provides additional control over the key used to encrypt data at rest. This feature is often applicable to customers with special compliance requirements to manage data encryption keys using a key vault.

policies.name: 67121cc7-ff39-4ab8-b7e3-95b84dab487d
policies.displayName: Azure AI Services resources should encrypt data at rest with a customer-managed key (CMK)
policies.description: Using customer-managed keys to encrypt data at rest provides more control over the key lifecycle, including rotation and management. This is particularly relevant for organizations with related compliance requirements. This is not assessed by default and should only be applied when required by compliance or restrictive policy requirements. If not enabled, the data will be encrypted using platform-managed keys. To implement this, update the 'Effect' parameter in the Security Policy for the applicable scope.

policies.name: 71ef260a-8f18-47b7-abcb-62d0673d94dc
policies.displayName: Azure AI Services resources should have key access disabled (disable local authentication)
policies.description: Key access (local authentication) is recommended to be disabled for security. Azure OpenAI Studio, typically used in development/testing, requires key access and will not function if key access is disabled. After disabling, Microsoft Entra ID becomes the only access method, which allows maintaining minimum privilege principle and granular control. Learn more at: https://aka.ms/AI/auth

policies.name: 037eea7a-bd0a-46c5-9a66-03aea78705d3
policies.displayName: Azure AI Services resources should restrict network access
policies.description: By restricting network access, you can ensure that only allowed networks can access the service. This can be achieved by configuring network rules so that only applications from allowed networks can access the Azure AI service.

policies.name: d6759c02-b87f-42b7-892e-71b3f471d782
policies.displayName: Azure AI Services resources should use Azure Private Link
policies.description: Azure Private Link lets you connect your virtual network to Azure services without a public IP address at the source or destination. The Private Link platform reduces data leakage risks by handling the connectivity between the consumer and services over the Azure backbone network. Learn more about private links at: https://aka.ms/AzurePrivateLink/Overview

policies.name: 051cba44-2429-45b9-9649-46cec11c7119
policies.displayName: Azure API for FHIR should use a customer-managed key to encrypt data at rest
policies.description: Use a customer-managed key to control the encryption at rest of the data stored in Azure API for FHIR when this is a regulatory or compliance requirement. Customer-managed keys also deliver double encryption by adding a second layer of encryption on top of the default one done with service-managed keys.

policies.name: 1ee56206-5dd1-42ab-b02d-8aae8b1634ce
policies.displayName: Azure API for FHIR should use private link
policies.description: Azure API for FHIR should have at least one approved private endpoint connection. Clients in a virtual network can securely access resources that have private endpoint connections through private links. For more information, visit: https://aka.ms/fhir-privatelink.

policies.name: 1dc2fc00-2245-4143-99f4-874c937f13ef
policies.displayName: Azure API Management platform version should be stv2
policies.description: Azure API Management stv1 compute platform version will be retired effective 31 August 2024, and these instances should be migrated to stv2 compute platform for continued support. Learn more at https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/api-management/breaking-changes/stv1-platform-retirement-august-2024

policies.name: c3a8e4bd-b215-4c99-bd53-92f8d7ea65f7
policies.displayName: Azure Application Gateway for Containers must have security policies
policies.description: Ensures Application Gateway for Containers has at least one security policy configured

policies.name: ff1f1879-a60d-4f23-9641-41e7391ec19a
policies.displayName: Azure Application Gateway should be deployed with Azure WAF
policies.description: Requires Azure Application Gateway resources to be deployed with Azure WAF.

policies.name: 8a04f872-51e9-4313-97fb-fc1c3543011c
policies.displayName: Azure Application Gateway should have Resource logs enabled
policies.description: Enable Resource logs for Azure Application Gateway (plus WAF) and stream to a Log Analytics workspace. Get detailed visibility into inbound web traffic and actions taken to mitigate attacks.

policies.name: 6b2122c1-8120-4ff5-801b-17625a355590
policies.displayName: Azure Arc enabled Kubernetes clusters should have the Azure Policy extension installed
policies.description: The Azure Policy extension for Azure Arc provides at-scale enforcements and safeguards on your Arc enabled Kubernetes clusters in a centralized, consistent manner. Learn more at https://aka.ms/akspolicydoc.

policies.name: 7eab1da3-2bf0-4ff0-8303-1a4277c380e8
policies.displayName: Azure Arc Private Link Scopes should be configured with a private endpoint
policies.description: Azure Private Link lets you connect your virtual networks to Azure services without a public IP address at the source or destination. The Private Link platform handles the connectivity between the consumer and services over the Azure backbone network. By mapping private endpoints to Azure Arc Private Link Scopes, data leakage risks are reduced. Learn more about private links at: https://aka.ms/arc/privatelink.

policies.name: 898f2439-3333-4713-af25-f1d78bc50556
policies.displayName: Azure Arc Private Link Scopes should disable public network access
policies.description: Disabling public network access improves security by ensuring that Azure Arc resources cannot connect via the public internet. Creating private endpoints can limit exposure of Azure Arc resources. Learn more at: https://aka.ms/arc/privatelink.

policies.name: 12e7176a-4919-47ef-922b-34eda4c7f0ce
policies.displayName: Azure Arc-enabled kubernetes clusters should be configured with an Azure Arc Private Link Scope
policies.description: Azure Private Link lets you connect your virtual networks to Azure services without a public IP address at the source or destination. The Private Link platform handles the connectivity between the consumer and services over the Azure backbone network. By mapping Azure Arc-enabled servers to an Azure Arc Private Link Scope that is configured with a private endpoint, data leakage risks are reduced. Learn more about private links at: https://aka.ms/arc/privatelink.

policies.name: 73868911-4f4a-444f-adbd-5382bf70208a
policies.displayName: Azure Arc-enabled Kubernetes clusters should have the Open Service Mesh extension installed
policies.description: Open Service Mesh extension provides all standard service mesh capabilities for security, traffic management and observability of application services. Learn more here: https://aka.ms/arc-osm-doc

policies.name: a8e653d9-b5d4-48a0-afe6-14d881f9ee9a
policies.displayName: Azure Arc-enabled Kubernetes clusters should have the Strimzi Kafka extension installed
policies.description: Strimzi Kafka extension provides the operators to install Kafka for building real-time data pipelines and streaming applications with security and observability capabilities. Learn more here: https://aka.ms/arc-strimzikafka-doc.

policies.name: efa3f296-ff2b-4f38-bc0d-5ef12c965b68
policies.displayName: Azure Arc-enabled servers should be configured with an Azure Arc Private Link Scope
policies.description: Azure Private Link lets you connect your virtual networks to Azure services without a public IP address at the source or destination. The Private Link platform handles the connectivity between the consumer and services over the Azure backbone network. By mapping Azure Arc-enabled servers to an Azure Arc Private Link Scope that is configured with a private endpoint, data leakage risks are reduced. Learn more about private links at: https://aka.ms/arc/privatelink.

policies.name: 5e7e928c-8693-4a23-9bf3-1c77b9a8fe97
policies.displayName: Azure Attestation providers should disable public network access
policies.description: To improve the security of Azure Attestation Service, ensure that it isn't exposed to the public internet and can only be accessed from a private endpoint. Disable the public network access property as described in aka.ms/azureattestation. This option disables access from any public address space outside the Azure IP range, and denies all logins that match IP or virtual network-based firewall rules. This reduces data leakage risks.

policies.name: 7b256a2d-058b-41f8-bed9-3f870541c40a
policies.displayName: Azure Attestation providers should use private endpoints
policies.description: Private endpoints provide a way to connect Azure Attestation providers to your Azure resources without sending traffic over the public internet. By preventing public access, private endpoints help protect against undesired anonymous access.

policies.name: 48c5f1cb-14ad-4797-8e3b-f78ab3f8d700
policies.displayName: Azure Automation account should have local authentication method disabled
policies.description: Disabling local authentication methods improves security by ensuring that Azure Automation accounts exclusively require Azure Active Directory identities for authentication.

policies.name: 56a5ee18-2ae6-4810-86f7-18e39ce5629b
policies.displayName: Azure Automation accounts should use customer-managed keys to encrypt data at rest
policies.description: Use customer-managed keys to manage the encryption at rest of your Azure Automation Accounts. By default, customer data is encrypted with service-managed keys, but customer-managed keys are commonly required to meet regulatory compliance standards. Customer-managed keys enable the data to be encrypted with an Azure Key Vault key created and owned by you. You have full control and responsibility for the key lifecycle, including rotation and management. Learn more at https://aka.ms/automation-cmk.

policies.name: 013e242c-8828-4970-87b3-ab247555486d
policies.displayName: Azure Backup should be enabled for Virtual Machines
policies.description: Ensure protection of your Azure Virtual Machines by enabling Azure Backup. Azure Backup is a secure and cost effective data protection solution for Azure.

policies.name: d6588149-9f06-462c-a076-56aece45b5ba
policies.displayName: Azure Backup Vaults should use customer-managed keys for encrypting backup data. Also an option to enforce Infra Encryption.
policies.description: This policy follows the 'effect' if Encryption Settings are enabled for Backup vaults in the scope. Additionally, option to check if Backup Vault also has Infrastructure Encryption enabled. Learn more at https://aka.ms/az-backup-vault-encryption-at-rest-with-cmk. Please note that when 'Deny' effect is used, it would need you to enable Encryption Settings on the existing Backup Vaults in order to allow other update operations on the vault go through.

policies.name: 99e9ccd8-3db9-4592-b0d1-14b1715a4d8a
policies.displayName: Azure Batch account should use customer-managed keys to encrypt data
policies.description: Use customer-managed keys to manage the encryption at rest of your Batch account's data. By default, customer data is encrypted with service-managed keys, but customer-managed keys are commonly required to meet regulatory compliance standards. Customer-managed keys enable the data to be encrypted with an Azure Key Vault key created and owned by you. You have full control and responsibility for the key lifecycle, including rotation and management. Learn more at https://aka.ms/Batch-CMK.

policies.name: 1760f9d4-7206-436e-a28f-d9f3a5c8a227
policies.displayName: Azure Batch pools should have disk encryption enabled
policies.description: Enabling Azure Batch disk encryption ensures that data is always encrypted at rest on your Azure Batch compute node. Learn more about disk encryption in Batch at https://docs.microsoft.com/azure/batch/disk-encryption.

policies.name: 09aa11bb-87ec-409f-bf0b-49b7c1561a87
policies.displayName: Azure Cache for Redis Enterprise should use customer-managed keys for encrypting disk data
policies.description: Use customer-managed keys (CMK) to manage the encryption at rest of your on-disk data. By default, customer data is encrypted with platform-managed keys (PMK), but customer-managed keys are commonly required to meet regulatory compliance standards. Customer-managed keys enable the data to be encrypted with an Azure Key Vault key created and owned by you. You have full control and responsibility for the key lifecycle, including rotation and management. Learn more at https://aka.ms/RedisCMK.

policies.name: 960e650e-9ce3-4316-9590-8ee2c016ca2f
policies.displayName: Azure Cache for Redis Enterprise should use private link
policies.description: Private endpoints lets you connect your virtual network to Azure services without a public IP address at the source or destination. By mapping private endpoints to your Azure Cache for Redis Enterprise instances, data leakage risks are reduced. Learn more at: https://docs.microsoft.com/azure/azure-cache-for-redis/cache-private-link.

policies.name: 470baccb-7e51-4549-8b1a-3e5be069f663
policies.displayName: Azure Cache for Redis should disable public network access
policies.description: Disabling public network access improves security by ensuring that the Azure Cache for Redis isn't exposed on the public internet. You can limit exposure of your Azure Cache for Redis by creating private endpoints instead. Learn more at: https://docs.microsoft.com/azure/azure-cache-for-redis/cache-private-link.

policies.name: 3827af20-8f80-4b15-8300-6db0873ec901
policies.displayName: Azure Cache for Redis should not use access keys for authentication
policies.description: Not using local authentication methods like access keys and using more secure alternatives like Microsoft Entra ID (recommended) improves security for your Azure Cache for Redis. Learn more at aka.ms/redis/disableAccessKeyAuthentication

policies.name: 7803067c-7d34-46e3-8c79-0ca68fc4036d
policies.displayName: Azure Cache for Redis should use private link
policies.description: Private endpoints lets you connect your virtual network to Azure services without a public IP address at the source or destination. By mapping private endpoints to your Azure Cache for Redis instances, data leakage risks are reduced. Learn more at: https://docs.microsoft.com/azure/azure-cache-for-redis/cache-private-link.

policies.name: 8af8f826-edcb-4178-b35f-851ea6fea615
policies.displayName: Azure Container Instance container group should deploy into a virtual network
policies.description: Secure communication between your containers with Azure Virtual Networks. When you specify a virtual network, resources within the virtual network can securely and privately communicate with each other.

policies.name: 0aa61e00-0a01-4a3c-9945-e93cffedf0e6
policies.displayName: Azure Container Instance container group should use customer-managed key for encryption
policies.description: Secure your containers with greater flexibility using customer-managed keys. When you specify a customer-managed key, that key is used to protect and control access to the key that encrypts your data. Using customer-managed keys provides additional capabilities to control rotation of the key encryption key or cryptographically erase data.

policies.name: 862e97cf-49fc-4a5c-9de4-40d4e2e7c8eb
policies.displayName: Azure Cosmos DB accounts should have firewall rules
policies.description: Firewall rules should be defined on your Azure Cosmos DB accounts to prevent traffic from unauthorized sources. Accounts that have at least one IP rule defined with the virtual network filter enabled are deemed compliant. Accounts disabling public access are also deemed compliant.

policies.name: 12339a85-a25c-4f17-9f82-4766f13f5c4c
policies.displayName: Azure Cosmos DB accounts should not allow traffic from all Azure data centers
policies.description: Disallow the IP Firewall rule, '0.0.0.0', which allows for all traffic from any Azure data centers. Learn more at https://aka.ms/cosmosdb-firewall

policies.name: 9d83ccb1-f313-46ce-9d39-a198bfdb51a0
policies.displayName: Azure Cosmos DB accounts should not exceed the maximum number of days allowed since last account key regeneration.
policies.description: Regenerate your keys in the specified time to keep your data more protected.

policies.name: 1f905d99-2ab7-462c-a6b0-f709acca6c8f
policies.displayName: Azure Cosmos DB accounts should use customer-managed keys to encrypt data at rest
policies.description: Use customer-managed keys to manage the encryption at rest of your Azure Cosmos DB. By default, the data is encrypted at rest with service-managed keys, but customer-managed keys are commonly required to meet regulatory compliance standards. Customer-managed keys enable the data to be encrypted with an Azure Key Vault key created and owned by you. You have full control and responsibility for the key lifecycle, including rotation and management. Learn more at https://aka.ms/cosmosdb-cmk.

policies.name: 0473574d-2d43-4217-aefe-941fcdf7e684
policies.displayName: Azure Cosmos DB allowed locations
policies.description: This policy enables you to restrict the locations your organization can specify when deploying Azure Cosmos DB resources. Use to enforce your geo-compliance requirements.

policies.name: 4750c32b-89c0-46af-bfcb-2e4541a818d5
policies.displayName: Azure Cosmos DB key based metadata write access should be disabled
policies.description: This policy enables you to ensure all Azure Cosmos DB accounts disable key based metadata write access.

policies.name: 797b37f7-06b8-444c-b1ad-fc62867f335a
policies.displayName: Azure Cosmos DB should disable public network access
policies.description: Disabling public network access improves security by ensuring that your CosmosDB account isn't exposed on the public internet. Creating private endpoints can limit exposure of your CosmosDB account. Learn more at: https://docs.microsoft.com/azure/cosmos-db/how-to-configure-private-endpoints#blocking-public-network-access-during-account-creation.

policies.name: 0b7ef78e-a035-4f23-b9bd-aff122a1b1cf
policies.displayName: Azure Cosmos DB throughput should be limited
policies.description: This policy enables you to restrict the maximum throughput your organization can specify when creating Azure Cosmos DB databases and containers through the resource provider. It blocks the creation of autoscale resources.

policies.name: c349d81b-9985-44ae-a8da-ff98d108ede8
policies.displayName: Azure Data Box jobs should enable double encryption for data at rest on the device
policies.description: Enable a second layer of software-based encryption for data at rest on the device. The device is already protected via Advanced Encryption Standard 256-bit encryption for data at rest. This option adds a second layer of data encryption.

policies.name: 86efb160-8de7-451d-bc08-5d475b0aadae
policies.displayName: Azure Data Box jobs should use a customer-managed key to encrypt the device unlock password
policies.description: Use a customer-managed key to control the encryption of the device unlock password for Azure Data Box. Customer-managed keys also help manage access to the device unlock password by the Data Box service in order to prepare the device and copy data in an automated manner. The data on the device itself is already encrypted at rest with Advanced Encryption Standard 256-bit encryption, and the device unlock password is encrypted by default with a Microsoft managed key.

policies.name: f7735886-8927-431f-b201-c953922512b8
policies.displayName: Azure Data Explorer cluster should use private link
policies.description: Azure Private Link lets you connect your virtual network to Azure services without a public IP address at the source or destination. The Private Link platform handles the connectivity between the consumer and services over the Azure backbone network. By mapping private endpoints to your Azure Data Explorer cluster, data leakage risks are reduced. Learn more about private links at: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/data-explorer/security-network-private-endpoint.

policies.name: 81e74cea-30fd-40d5-802f-d72103c2aaaa
policies.displayName: Azure Data Explorer encryption at rest should use a customer-managed key
policies.description: Enabling encryption at rest using a customer-managed key on your Azure Data Explorer cluster provides additional control over the key being used by the encryption at rest. This feature is oftentimes applicable to customers with special compliance requirements and requires a Key Vault to managing the keys.

policies.name: 1fec9658-933f-4b3e-bc95-913ed22d012b
policies.displayName: Azure Data Explorer should use a SKU that supports private link
policies.description: With supported SKUs, Azure Private Link lets you connect your virtual network to Azure services without a public IP address at the source or destination. The Private Link platform handles the connectivity between the consumer and services over the Azure backbone network. By mapping private endpoints to apps, you can reduce data leakage risks. Learn more about private links at: https://aka.ms/private-link.

policies.name: 4ec52d6d-beb7-40c4-9a9e-fe753254690e
policies.displayName: Azure data factories should be encrypted with a customer-managed key
policies.description: Use customer-managed keys to manage the encryption at rest of your Azure Data Factory. By default, customer data is encrypted with service-managed keys, but customer-managed keys are commonly required to meet regulatory compliance standards. Customer-managed keys enable the data to be encrypted with an Azure Key Vault key created and owned by you. You have full control and responsibility for the key lifecycle, including rotation and management. Learn more at https://aka.ms/adf-cmk.

policies.name: 85bb39b5-2f66-49f8-9306-77da3ac5130f
policies.displayName: Azure Data Factory integration runtime should have a limit for number of cores
policies.description: To manage your resources and costs, limit the number of cores for an integration runtime.

policies.name: 6809a3d0-d354-42fb-b955-783d207c62a8
policies.displayName: Azure Data Factory linked service resource type should be in allow list
policies.description: Define the allow list of Azure Data Factory linked service types. Restricting allowed resource types enables control over the boundary of data movement. For example, restrict a scope to only allow blob storage with Data Lake Storage Gen1 and Gen2 for analytics or a scope to only allow SQL and Kusto access for real-time queries.

policies.name: 127ef6d7-242f-43b3-9eef-947faf1725d0
policies.displayName: Azure Data Factory linked services should use Key Vault for storing secrets
policies.description: To ensure secrets (such as connection strings) are managed securely, require users to provide secrets using an Azure Key Vault instead of specifying them inline in linked services.

policies.name: f78ccdb4-7bf4-4106-8647-270491d2978a
policies.displayName: Azure Data Factory linked services should use system-assigned managed identity authentication when it is supported
policies.description: Using system-assigned managed identity when communicating with data stores via linked services avoids the use of less secured credentials such as passwords or connection strings.

policies.name: 77d40665-3120-4348-b539-3192ec808307
policies.displayName: Azure Data Factory should use a Git repository for source control
policies.description: Configure only your development data factory with Git integration. Changes to test and production should be deployed via CI/CD and should NOT have Git integration.  DO NOT apply this policy on your QA / Test / Production data factories.

policies.name: 8b0323be-cc25-4b61-935d-002c3798c6ea
policies.displayName: Azure Data Factory should use private link
policies.description: Azure Private Link lets you connect your virtual network to Azure services without a public IP address at the source or destination. The Private Link platform handles the connectivity between the consumer and services over the Azure backbone network. By mapping private endpoints to Azure Data Factory, data leakage risks are reduced. Learn more about private links at: https://docs.microsoft.com/azure/data-factory/data-factory-private-link.

policies.name: 51c1490f-3319-459c-bbbc-7f391bbed753
policies.displayName: Azure Databricks Clusters should disable public IP
policies.description: Disabling public IP of clusters in Azure Databricks Workspaces improves security by ensuring that the clusters aren't exposed on the public internet. Learn more at: https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/databricks/security/secure-cluster-connectivity.
