policies.name: 9f766f00-8d11-464e-80e1-4091d7874074
policies.displayName: Configure Storage account to use a private link connection
policies.description: Private endpoints connect your virtual network to Azure services without a public IP address at the source or destination. By mapping private endpoints to your storage account, you can reduce data leakage risks. Learn more about private links at - https://aka.ms/azureprivatelinkoverview

policies.name: a06d0189-92e8-4dba-b0c4-08d7669fce7d
policies.displayName: Configure storage accounts to disable public network access
policies.description: To improve the security of Storage Accounts, ensure that they aren't exposed to the public internet and can only be accessed from a private endpoint. Disable the public network access property as described in https://aka.ms/storageaccountpublicnetworkaccess. This option disables access from any public address space outside the Azure IP range, and denies all logins that match IP or virtual network-based firewall rules. This reduces data leakage risks.

policies.name: 41a72361-06e3-4e80-832a-690bd0708bc1
policies.displayName: Configure Storage Accounts to restrict network access through network ACL bypass configuration only.
policies.description: To improve the security of Storage Accounts, enable access only through network ACL bypass. This policy should be used in combination with a private endpoint for storage account access.

policies.name: 98903777-a9f6-47f5-90a9-acaf62ab01a8
policies.displayName: Configure subscriptions to enable service health alert monitoring rule
policies.description: Assignable at the subscription or management group level, this policy ensures that each subscription has a service health alert rule configured with alert conditions and mapping to action groups as specified in the policy parameters. By default creates a resource group, alert rule and action group configured to send emails to subscription owners for all service health events.

policies.name: e624c84f-2923-4437-9fd9-4115c6da3888
policies.displayName: Configure subscriptions to set up preview features
policies.description: This policy evaluates existing subscription's preview features. Subscriptions can be remediated to register to a new preview feature. New subscriptions will not be automatically registered.

policies.name: ac7891a4-ac7a-4ba0-9ae9-c923e5a225ee
policies.displayName: Configure Synapse workspaces to have auditing enabled
policies.description: To ensure the operations performed against your SQL assets are captured, Synapse workspaces should have auditing enabled. This is sometimes required for compliance with regulatory standards.

policies.name: 32ba8d30-07c0-4136-ab18-9a11bf4a67b7
policies.displayName: Configure Synapse workspaces to have auditing enabled to Log Analytics workspace
policies.description: To ensure the operations performed against your SQL assets are captured, Synapse workspaces should have auditing enabled. If auditing is not enabled, this policy will configure auditing events to flow to the specified Log Analytics workspace.

policies.name: 738949be-6fd2-46b9-b969-99b53712b192
policies.displayName: Configure Synapse Workspaces to use only Microsoft Entra identities for authentication
policies.description: Require and reconfigure Synapse Workspaces to use Microsoft Entra-only authentication. This policy doesn't block workspaces from being created with local authentication enabled. It does block local authentication from being enabled and re-enables Microsoft Entra-only authentication on resources after create. Consider using the 'Microsoft Entra-only authentication' initiative instead to require both. Learn more at: https://aka.ms/Synapse.

policies.name: c3624673-d2ff-48e0-b28c-5de1c6767c3c
policies.displayName: Configure Synapse Workspaces to use only Microsoft Entra identities for authentication during workspace creation
policies.description: Require and reconfigure Synapse Workspaces to be created with Microsoft Entra-only authentication. This policy doesn't block local authentication from being re-enabled on resources after create. Consider using the 'Microsoft Entra-only authentication' initiative instead to require both. Learn more at: https://aka.ms/Synapse.

policies.name: 242300d6-1bfc-4d64-8d01-cee583709ebd
policies.displayName: Configure the Microsoft Defender for SQL Log Analytics workspace
policies.description: Microsoft Defender for SQL collects events from the agent and uses them to provide security alerts and tailored hardening tasks (recommendations). Create a resource group and Log Analytics workspace in the same region as the machine.

policies.name: 6141c932-9384-44c6-a395-59e4c057d7c9
policies.displayName: Configure time zone on Windows machines.
policies.description: This policy creates a Guest Configuration assignment to set specified time zone on Windows virtual machines.

policies.name: f889cab7-da27-4c41-a3b0-de1f6f87c550
policies.displayName: Configure virtual machines to be onboarded to Azure Automanage
policies.description: Azure Automanage enrolls, configures, and monitors virtual machines with best practice as defined in the Microsoft Cloud Adoption Framework for Azure. Use this policy to apply Automanage to your selected scope.

policies.name: b025cfb4-3702-47c2-9110-87fe0cfcc99b
policies.displayName: Configure virtual machines to be onboarded to Azure Automanage with Custom Configuration Profile
policies.description: Azure Automanage enrolls, configures, and monitors virtual machines with best practice as defined in the Microsoft Cloud Adoption Framework for Azure. Use this policy to apply Automanage with your own customized Configuration Profile to your selected scope.

policies.name: 3e9965dc-cc13-47ca-8259-a4252fd0cf7b
policies.displayName: Configure virtual network to enable Flow Log and Traffic Analytics
policies.description: Traffic analytics and Flow logs can be enabled for all virtual networks hosted in a particular region with the settings provided during policy creation. This policy does not overwrite current setting for virtual networks that already have these feature enabled. Traffic analytics is a cloud-based solution that provides visibility into user and application activity in cloud networks.

policies.name: 052c180e-287d-44c3-86ef-01aeae2d9774
policies.displayName: Configure virtual networks to enforce workspace, storage account and retention interval for Flow logs and Traffic Analytics
policies.description: If a virtual network already has traffic analytics enabled, then, this policy will overwrite its existing settings with the ones provided during policy creation. Traffic analytics is a cloud-based solution that provides visibility into user and application activity in cloud networks.

policies.name: 3d9a4145-9197-45fa-afcd-84b887b4e2d3
policies.displayName: Configure Windows and Linux virtual machines to use Microsoft Entra ID for sign-in
policies.description: Deploys the Microsoft Entra ID login extension (AADLoginForWindows on Windows VMs, AADSSHLoginForLinux on Linux VMs) and enables a system-assigned managed identity on Azure virtual machines, so users can sign in with their Microsoft Entra credentials. Learn more at https://aka.ms/AzureADLoginVMs.

policies.name: c24c537f-2516-4c2f-aac5-2cd26baa3d26
policies.displayName: Configure Windows Arc Machines to be associated with a Data Collection Rule or a Data Collection Endpoint
policies.description: Deploy Association to link Windows Arc machines to the specified Data Collection Rule or the specified Data Collection Endpoint. The list of locations are updated over time as support is increased.

policies.name: ef9fe2ce-a588-4edd-829c-6247069dcfdb
policies.displayName: Configure Windows Arc-enabled machines to be associated with a Data Collection Rule for ChangeTracking and Inventory
policies.description: Deploy Association to link Windows Arc-enabled machines to specified Data Collection Rule to enable ChangeTracking and Inventory. The list of locations are updated over time as support is increased.

policies.name: a7acfae7-9497-4a3f-a3b5-a16a50abbe2f
policies.displayName: Configure Windows Arc-enabled machines to install AMA for ChangeTracking and Inventory
policies.description: Automate the deployment of Azure Monitor Agent extension on your Windows Arc-enabled machines for enabling ChangeTracking and Inventory. This policy will install the extension if the OS and region are supported and system-assigned managed identity is enabled, and skip install otherwise. Learn more: https://aka.ms/AMAOverview.

This policy will install the extension if the OS and region are supported and system-assigned managed identity is enabled, and skip install otherwise. Learn more: https://aka.ms/AMAOverview.

policies.displayName: Configure Windows Machines to be associated with a Data Collection Rule or a Data Collection Endpoint
policies.description: Deploy Association to link Windows virtual machines, virtual machine scale sets, and Arc machines to the specified Data Collection Rule or the specified Data Collection Endpoint. The list of locations and OS images are updated over time as support is increased.

policies.description: Automate the deployment of Azure Monitor Agent extension on your Windows virtual machine scale sets for collecting telemetry data from the guest OS. This policy will install the extension if the OS and region are supported and system-assigned managed identity is enabled, and skip install otherwise. Learn more: https://aka.ms/AMAOverview.

policies.description: Deploy Association to link Windows virtual machines to specified Data Collection Rule to enable ChangeTracking and Inventory. The list of locations and OS images are updated over time as support is increased.

policies.displayName: Configure Windows Virtual Machines to be associated with a Data Collection Rule or a Data Collection Endpoint
policies.description: Deploy Association to link Windows virtual machines to the specified Data Collection Rule or the specified Data Collection Endpoint. The list of locations and OS images are updated over time as support is increased.

policies.displayName: Configure workstations to check for digital certificates

policies.name: 13502221-8df0-4414-9937-de9c5c4e396b
policies.displayName: Configure your Storage account public access to be disallowed
policies.description: Anonymous public read access to containers and blobs in Azure Storage is a convenient way to share data but might present security risks. To prevent data breaches caused by undesired anonymous access, Microsoft recommends preventing public access to a storage account unless your scenario requires it.

policies.name: c36a325b-ae04-4863-ad4f-19c6678f8e08
policies.displayName: Configure your Storage account to enable blob versioning
policies.description: You can enable Blob storage versioning to automatically maintain previous versions of an object. When blob versioning is enabled, you can access earlier versions of a blob to recover your data if it's modified or deleted.

policies.name: 8bb40df9-23e4-4175-5db3-8dba86349b73
policies.displayName: Confirm quality and integrity of PII
policies.description: CMA_C1821 - Confirm quality and integrity of PII

policies.displayName: Conform to FICAM-issued profiles
policies.description: CMA_C1350 - Conform to FICAM-issued profiles

policies.name: 5345bb39-67dc-4960-a1bf-427e16b9a0bd
policies.displayName: Connection throttling should be enabled for PostgreSQL database servers
policies.description: This policy helps audit any PostgreSQL databases in your environment without Connection throttling enabled. This setting enables temporary connection throttling per IP for too many invalid password login failures.

policies.name: 8b346db6-85af-419b-8557-92cee2c0f9bb
policies.displayName: Container App environments should use network injection
policies.description: Container Apps environments should use virtual network injection to: 1.Isolate Container Apps from the public internet 2.Enable network integration with resources on-premises or in other Azure virtual networks 3.Achieve more granular control over network traffic flowing to and from the environment.

policies.name: 7c9f3fbb-739d-4844-8e42-97e3be6450e0
policies.displayName: Container App should configure with volume mount
policies.description: Enforce the use of volume mounts for Container Apps to ensure availability of persistent storage capacity.

policies.name: d074ddf8-01a5-4b5e-a2b8-964aed452c0a
policies.displayName: Container Apps environment should disable public network access
policies.description: Disable public network access to improve security by exposing the Container Apps environment through an internal load balancer. This removes the need for a public IP address and prevents internet access to all Container Apps within the environment.

policies.name: 783ea2a8-b8fd-46be-896a-9ae79643a0b1
policies.displayName: Container Apps should disable external network access
policies.description: Disable external network access to your Container Apps by enforcing internal-only ingress. This will ensure inbound communication for Container Apps is limited to callers within the Container Apps environment.

policies.name: 0e80e269-43a4-4ae9-b5bc-178126b8a5cb
policies.displayName: Container Apps should only be accessible over HTTPS
policies.description: Use of HTTPS ensures server/service authentication and protects data in transit from network layer eavesdropping attacks. Disabling 'allowInsecure' will result in the automatic redirection of requests from HTTP to HTTPS connections for container apps.

policies.name: 5b9159ae-1701-4a6f-9a7a-aa9c8ddd0580
policies.displayName: Container registries should be encrypted with a customer-managed key
policies.description: Use customer-managed keys to manage the encryption at rest of the contents of your registries. By default, the data is encrypted at rest with service-managed keys, but customer-managed keys are commonly required to meet regulatory compliance standards. Customer-managed keys enable the data to be encrypted with an Azure Key Vault key created and owned by you. You have full control and responsibility for the key lifecycle, including rotation and management. Learn more at https://aka.ms/acr/CMK.

policies.name: 9f2dea28-e834-476c-99c5-3507b4728395
policies.displayName: Container registries should have anonymous authentication disabled.
policies.description: Disable anonymous pull for your registry so that data is not accessible by unauthenticated user. Disabling local authentication methods like admin user, repository scoped access tokens and anonymous pull improves security by ensuring that container registries exclusively require Azure Active Directory identities for authentication. Learn more at: https://aka.ms/acr/authentication.

policies.name: 42781ec6-6127-4c30-bdfa-fb423a0047d3
policies.displayName: Container registries should have ARM audience token authentication disabled.
policies.description: Disable Azure Active Directory ARM audience tokens for authentication to your registry. Only Azure Container Registry (ACR) audience tokens will be used for authentication. This will ensure only tokens meant for usage on the registry can be used for authentication. Disabling ARM audience tokens does not affect admin user's or scoped access tokens' authentication. Learn more at: https://aka.ms/acr/authentication.

policies.name: 524b0254-c285-4903-bee6-bb8126cde579
policies.displayName: Container registries should have exports disabled
policies.description: Disabling exports improves security by ensuring data in a registry is accessed solely via the dataplane ('docker pull'). Data cannot be moved out of the registry via 'acr import' or via 'acr transfer'. In order to disable exports, public network access must be disabled. Learn more at: https://aka.ms/acr/export-policy.

policies.name: dc921057-6b28-4fbe-9b83-f7bec05db6c2
policies.displayName: Container registries should have local admin account disabled.
policies.description: Disable admin account for your registry so that it is not accessible by local admin. Disabling local authentication methods like admin user, repository scoped access tokens and anonymous pull improves security by ensuring that container registries exclusively require Azure Active Directory identities for authentication. Learn more at: https://aka.ms/acr/authentication.

policies.name: ff05e24e-195c-447e-b322-5e90c9f9f366
policies.displayName: Container registries should have repository scoped access token disabled.
policies.description: Disable repository scoped access tokens for your registry so that repositories are not accessible by tokens. Disabling local authentication methods like admin user, repository scoped access tokens and anonymous pull improves security by ensuring that container registries exclusively require Azure Active Directory identities for authentication. Learn more at: https://aka.ms/acr/authentication.

policies.name: bd560fc0-3c69-498a-ae9f-aa8eb7de0e13
policies.displayName: Container registries should have SKUs that support Private Links
policies.description: Azure Private Link lets you connect your virtual network to Azure services without a public IP address at the source or destination. The private link platform handles the connectivity between the consumer and services over the Azure backbone network. By mapping private endpoints to your container registries instead of the entire service, data leakage risks are reduced. Learn more at: https://aka.ms/acr/private-link.

policies.name: d0793b48-0edc-4296-a390-4c75d1bdfd71
policies.displayName: Container registries should not allow unrestricted network access
policies.description: Azure container registries by default accept connections over the internet from hosts on any network. To protect your registries from potential threats, allow access from only specific private endpoints, public IP addresses or address ranges. If your registry doesn't have network rules configured, it will appear in the unhealthy resources. Learn more about Container Registry network rules here: https://aka.ms/acr/privatelink, https://aka.ms/acr/portal/public-network and https://aka.ms/acr/vnet.

policies.name: 84497762-32b6-4ab3-80b6-732ea48b85a2
policies.displayName: Container registries should prevent cache rule creation
policies.description: Disable cache rule creation for your Azure Container Registry to prevent pull through cache pulls. Learn more at: https://aka.ms/acr/cache.

policies.name: e8eef0a8-67cf-4eb4-9386-14b0e78733d4
policies.displayName: Container registries should use private link
policies.description: Azure Private Link lets you connect your virtual network to Azure services without a public IP address at the source or destination. The private link platform handles the connectivity between the consumer and services over the Azure backbone network.By mapping private endpoints to your container registries instead of the entire service, you'll also be protected against data leakage risks. Learn more at: https://aka.ms/acr/private-link.

policies.name: 696cb1d3-2dcf-4b44-aa7a-caccd18b1b96
policies.displayName: Container Registry should restrict external private endpoints.
policies.description: This policy applies exclusively to Mission Platform products and services; usage outside of these scopes is not supported. It blocks approval of private endpoint connections to Container Registries from subscriptions outside the mission tenant (unless explicitly excluded) to preserve enclave boundaries and reduce data exposure risk. Learn more at https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/container-registry/container-registry-private-link.

policies.name: 0fea8f8a-4169-495d-8307-30ec335f387d
policies.displayName: CORS should not allow every domain to access your API for FHIR
policies.description: Cross-Origin Resource Sharing (CORS) should not allow all domains to access your API for FHIR. To protect your API for FHIR, remove access for all domains and explicitly define the domains allowed to connect.

policies.name: fe1c9040-c46a-4e81-9aea-c7850fbb3aa6
policies.displayName: CORS should not allow every domain to access your FHIR Service
policies.description: Cross-Origin Resource Sharing (CORS) should not allow all domains to access your FHIR Service. To protect your FHIR Service, remove access for all domains and explicitly define the domains allowed to connect.

policies.name: 50553764-7777-43cf-bf12-8647e0b9ba01
policies.displayName: CORS should not allow every resource to access your map account.
policies.description: Cross-Origin Resource Sharing (CORS) should not allow all domains to access your map account. Allow only required domains to interact with your map account.

policies.name: 5450f5bd-9c72-4390-a9c4-a7aba4edfdd2
policies.displayName: Cosmos DB database accounts should have local authentication methods disabled
policies.description: Disabling local authentication methods improves security by ensuring that Cosmos DB database accounts exclusively require Azure Active Directory identities for authentication. Learn more at: https://docs.microsoft.com/azure/cosmos-db/how-to-setup-rbac#disable-local-auth.

policies.name: e0a2b1a3-f7f9-4569-807f-2a9edebdf4d9
policies.displayName: Cosmos DB should use a virtual network service endpoint
policies.description: This policy audits any Cosmos DB not configured to use a virtual network service endpoint.

policies.name: 58440f8a-10c5-4151-bdce-dfbaad4a20b7
policies.displayName: CosmosDB accounts should use private link
policies.description: Azure Private Link lets you connect your virtual network to Azure services without a public IP address at the source or destination. The Private Link platform handles the connectivity between the consumer and services over the Azure backbone network. By mapping private endpoints to your CosmosDB account, data leakage risks are reduced. Learn more about private links at: https://docs.microsoft.com/azure/cosmos-db/how-to-configure-private-endpoints.

policies.name: ea79b84d-f538-475d-a6ef-7951747a3455
policies.displayName: CosmosDB should restrict external private endpoints access
policies.description: This policy applies exclusively to Mission Platform products and services; usage outside of these scopes is not supported. This policy enforces restrictions on external private endpoints linked to Cosmos DB to maintain network isolation and prevent unauthorized cross-tenant access.

policies.name: 65e3adf0-0793-4cd2-af1f-134216ad5ce1
policies.displayName: CosmosDB should restrict public access but allow access from certain IP addresses
policies.description: This policy applies exclusively to Mission Platform products and services; usage outside of these scopes is not supported. This policy restricts Cosmos DB public network access while permitting connectivity from designated IP address ranges required for essential platform operations.

Customer-managed keys enable the data to be encrypted with an Azure Key Vault key created and owned by you, with full control and responsibility, including rotation and management.

policies.name: 0602787f-9896-402a-a6e1-39ee63ee435e
policies.displayName: Event Hub Namespaces should disable public network access
policies.description: Azure Event Hub should have public network access disabled. Disabling public network access improves security by ensuring that the resource isn't exposed on the public internet. You can limit exposure of your resources by creating private endpoints instead. Learn more at: https://docs.microsoft.com/azure/event-hubs/private-link-service

policies.name: 836cd60e-87f3-4e6a-a27c-29d687f01a4c
policies.displayName: Event Hub namespaces should have double encryption enabled
policies.description: Enabling double encryption helps protect and safeguard your data to meet your organizational security and compliance commitments. When double encryption has been enabled, data in the storage account is encrypted twice, once at the service level and once at the infrastructure level, using two different encryption algorithms and two different keys.

policies.name: a1ad735a-e96f-45d2-a7b2-9a4932cab7ec
policies.displayName: Event Hub namespaces should use a customer-managed key for encryption
policies.description: Azure Event Hubs supports the option of encrypting data at rest with either Microsoft-managed keys (default) or customer-managed keys. Choosing to encrypt data using customer-managed keys enables you to assign, rotate, disable, and revoke access to the keys that Event Hub will use to encrypt data in your namespace. Note that Event Hub only supports encryption with customer-managed keys for namespaces in dedicated clusters.

policies.name: b8564268-eb4a-4337-89be-a19db070c59d
policies.displayName: Event Hub namespaces should use private link
policies.description: Azure Private Link lets you connect your virtual network to Azure services without a public IP address at the source or destination. The Private Link platform handles the connectivity between the consumer and services over the Azure backbone network. By mapping private endpoints to Event Hub namespaces, data leakage risks are reduced. Learn more at: https://docs.microsoft.com/azure/event-hubs/private-link-service.

policies.name: d63edb4a-c612-454d-b47d-191a724fcbf0
policies.displayName: Event Hub should use a virtual network service endpoint
policies.description: This policy audits any Event Hub not configured to use a virtual network service endpoint.

policies.name: 16fabb5c-7379-4433-8009-042066fa3a16
policies.displayName: Exclude Usage Costs Resources
policies.description: This policy enables you to exclude Usage Costs Resources. Usage costs include things like metered storage and Azure resources which are billed based on usage.

policies.name: c42dee8c-0202-4a12-bd8e-3e171cbf64dd
policies.displayName: FHIR Service should use a customer-managed key to encrypt data at rest
policies.description: Use a customer-managed key to control the encryption at rest of the data stored in Azure Health Data Services FHIR Service when this is a regulatory or compliance requirement. Customer-managed keys also deliver double encryption by adding a second layer of encryption on top of the default one done with service-managed keys.

policies.name: c251913d-7d24-4958-af87-478ed3b9ba41
policies.displayName: Flow logs should be configured for every network security group
policies.description: Audit for network security groups to verify if flow logs are configured. Enabling flow logs allows to log information about IP traffic flowing through network security group. It can be used for optimizing network flows, monitoring throughput, verifying compliance, detecting intrusions and more.

policies.name: 46388f67-373c-4018-98d3-2b83172dd13a
policies.displayName: Fluid Relay should use customer-managed keys to encrypt data at rest
policies.description: Use customer-managed keys to manage the encryption at rest of your Fluid Relay server. By default, customer data is encrypted with service-managed keys, but CMKs are commonly required to meet regulatory compliance standards. Customer-managed keys enable the data to be encrypted with an Azure Key Vault key created and owned by you, with full control and responsibility, including rotation and management. Learn more at https://docs.microsoft.com/azure/azure-fluid-relay/concepts/customer-managed-keys.

policies.name: 8791d062-ba96-4c34-b604-8538f7e30ca0
policies.displayName: Foundry model deployments should meet eligibility requirements
policies.description: Ensures that model deployments in Microsoft Foundry comply with organizational eligibility requirements based on model attributes, such as availability status (preview or GA) and distribution source

policies.name: aafe3651-cb78-4f68-9f81-e7e41509110f
policies.displayName: Foundry model deployments should only use approved models
policies.description: Ensures that model deployments in Microsoft Foundry only use models explicitly approved by the organization, based on configured model identifiers or publishers.

policies.name: 3e90a76f-8f87-4753-9f18-b40f206c2653
policies.displayName: Function app slots should be injected into a virtual network
policies.description: Injecting Function Apps in a virtual network unlocks advanced networking and security features and provides you with greater control over your network security configuration. Learn more at: https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/app-service/web-sites-integrate-with-vnet.

policies.name: 11c82d0c-db9f-4d7b-97c5-f3f9aa957da2
policies.displayName: Function app slots should disable public network access
policies.description: Disabling public network access improves security by ensuring that the Function app is not exposed on the public internet. Creating private endpoints can limit exposure of a Function App. Learn more at: https://aka.ms/app-service-private-endpoint.

policies.name: f380edf5-de79-4862-bd57-ee407d8bd8b6
policies.displayName: Function app slots should enable configuration routing to Azure Virtual Network
policies.description: By default, configuration traffic (image pull, content share, backup/restore) is not routed through regional VNET integration. For API < 2024-11-01, set 'vnetImagePullEnabled', 'vnetContentShareEnabled', 'vnetBackupRestoreEnabled' to true. For API >= 2024-11-01, set the corresponding 'outboundVnetRouting' properties or 'outboundVnetRouting.allTraffic' to true. Not for Flex/Consumption plans. Learn more: https://aka.ms/appservice-vnet-configuration-routing.

policies.name: cbe0e5eb-fea9-491d-ab20-a62cf049c5ae
policies.displayName: Function app slots should enable end to end encryption
policies.description: Enabling end to end encryption ensures front-end intra-cluster traffic between App Service front-ends and the workers running application workloads is encrypted.

policies.name: 75c42c42-dfb3-453d-8fd5-9f978e1b1106
policies.displayName: Function app slots should enable outbound application traffic routing to Azure Virtual Network
policies.description: By default, regional VNET integration routes only RFC1918 traffic. Set 'vnetRouteAllEnabled' (API < 2024-11-01) or 'outboundVnetRouting.applicationTraffic' (API >= 2024-11-01) to route application traffic via the virtual network. Alternatively, set 'outboundVnetRouting.allTraffic' to route all traffic. Configuration traffic is handled separately by the configuration routing policy. Not for Flex/Consumption plans.

policies.name: b95f146e-2721-4579-a04c-3852b66514bd
policies.displayName: Function app slots should have authentication enabled
policies.description: Azure App Service Authentication is a feature that can prevent anonymous HTTP requests from reaching the function app slot, or authenticate those that have tokens before they reach the function app slot.

policies.name: f123aa67-1877-4e49-9aa6-33b38fa0bfe4
policies.displayName: Function app slots should have Client Certificates (Incoming client certificates) enabled
policies.description: Client certificates allow for the app to request a certificate for incoming requests. Only clients that have a valid certificate will be able to reach the app. This policy applies to function app slots.

policies.name: d813ace4-60e4-4103-9f8e-28cc81393f36
policies.displayName: Function app slots should have local authentication methods disabled for FTP deployments
policies.description: Disabling local authentication methods for FTP deployments improves security by ensuring that function app slots exclusively require Microsoft Entra identities for authentication. Learn more at: https://aka.ms/app-service-disable-basic-auth.

policies.name: 98040f7d-f5c6-41e1-82e1-ece2abceac84
policies.displayName: Function app slots should have local authentication methods disabled for SCM site deployments
policies.description: Disabling local authentication methods for SCM sites improves security by ensuring that function app slots exclusively require Microsoft Entra identities for authentication. Learn more at: https://aka.ms/app-service-disable-basic-auth.

policies.name: 89691ef9-8c50-49a8-8950-9c7fba41699e
policies.displayName: Function app slots should have remote debugging turned off
policies.description: Remote debugging requires inbound ports to be opened on Function apps. Remote debugging should be turned off.

policies.name: 2b8d966c-439e-4008-8c91-9c782b72aa9a
policies.displayName: Function app slots should have resource logs enabled
policies.description: Audit enabling of resource logs on the function app slot. This enables you to recreate activity trails for investigation purposes if a security incident occurs or your network is compromised.

policies.name: a1a22235-dd10-4062-bd55-7d62778f41b0
policies.displayName: Function app slots should not have CORS configured to allow every resource to access your apps
policies.description: Cross-Origin Resource Sharing (CORS) should not allow all domains to access your Function app. Allow only required domains to interact with your Function app.

policies.displayName: Function app slots should only be accessible over HTTPS

policies.displayName: Function app slots should provide an auto-generated domain name label scope
policies.description: Providing an auto-generated domain name label scope for your app ensures that the app can be accessed via a unique URL. For more information, see https://aka.ms/app-service-autoGeneratedDomainNameLabelScope.

policies.description: The content directory of a Function app should be located on an Azure file share. policies.displayName: HPC Cache accounts should use customer-managed key for encryption

You have full control and responsibility for the key lifecycle, including rotation and management.

policies.name: 9ace2dbc-4b71-48b6-b2a7-428b0b2e3944
policies.displayName: IoT Central should use private link
policies.description: Azure Private Link lets you connect your virtual network to Azure services without a public IP address at the source or destination. The private link platform handles the connectivity between the consumer and services over the Azure backbone network. By mapping private endpoints to your IoT Central application instead of the entire service, you'll reduce your data leakage risks. Learn more about private links at: https://aka.ms/iotcentral-network-security-using-pe.

policies.name: d82101f3-f3ce-4fc5-8708-4c09f4009546
policies.displayName: IoT Hub device provisioning service instances should disable public network access
policies.description: Disabling public network access improves security by ensuring that IoT Hub device provisioning service instance isn't exposed on the public internet. Creating private endpoints can limit exposure of the IoT Hub device provisioning instances. Learn more at: https://aka.ms/iotdpsvnet.

policies.name: df39c015-56a4-45de-b4a3-efe77bed320d
policies.displayName: IoT Hub device provisioning service instances should use private link
policies.description: Azure Private Link lets you connect your virtual network to Azure services without a public IP address at the source or destination. The Private Link platform handles the connectivity between the consumer and services over the Azure backbone network. By mapping private endpoints to the IoT Hub device provisioning service, data leakage risks are reduced. Learn more about private links at: https://aka.ms/iotdpsvnet.

policies.name: 56fd377d-098c-4f02-8406-81eb055902b8
policies.displayName: IP firewall rules on Azure Synapse workspaces should be removed
policies.description: Removing all IP firewall rules improves security by ensuring your Azure Synapse workspace can only be accessed from a private endpoint. This configuration audits creation of firewall rules that allow public network access on the workspace.

policies.name: bd352bd5-2853-4985-bf0d-73806b4a5744
policies.displayName: IP Forwarding on your virtual machine should be disabled
policies.description: Enabling IP forwarding on a virtual machine's NIC allows the machine to receive traffic addressed to other destinations. IP forwarding is rarely required (e.g., when using the VM as a network virtual appliance), and therefore, this should be reviewed by the network security team.

policies.name: 152b15f7-8e1f-4c1f-ab71-8c010ba5dbc0
policies.displayName: Key Vault keys should have an expiration date
policies.description: Cryptographic keys should have a defined expiration date and not be permanent. Keys that are valid forever provide a potential attacker with more time to compromise the key. It is a recommended security practice to set expiration dates on cryptographic keys.

policies.name: 98728c90-32c7-4049-8429-847dc0f4fe37
policies.displayName: Key Vault secrets should have an expiration date
policies.description: Secrets should have a defined expiration date and not be permanent. Secrets that are valid forever provide a potential attacker with more time to compromise them. It is a recommended security practice to set expiration dates on secrets.

policies.name: ea4d6841-2173-4317-9747-ff522a45120f
policies.displayName: Key Vault should use a virtual network service endpoint
policies.description: This policy audits any Key Vault not configured to use a virtual network service endpoint.

policies.name: 0b60c0b2-2dc2-4e1c-b5c9-abbed971de53
policies.displayName: Key vaults should have deletion protection enabled
policies.description: Malicious deletion of a key vault can lead to permanent data loss. You can prevent permanent data loss by enabling purge protection and soft delete. Purge protection protects you from insider attacks by enforcing a mandatory retention period for soft deleted key vaults. No one inside your organization or Microsoft will be able to purge your key vaults during the soft delete retention period. Keep in mind that key vaults created after September 1st 2019 have soft-delete enabled by default.

policies.name: 1e66c121-a66a-4b1f-9b83-0fd99bf0fc2d
policies.displayName: Key vaults should have soft delete enabled
policies.description: Deleting a key vault without soft delete enabled permanently deletes all secrets, keys, and certificates stored in the key vault. Accidental deletion of a key vault can lead to permanent data loss. Soft delete allows you to recover an accidentally deleted key vault for a configurable retention period.

policies.name: 587c79fe-dd04-4a5e-9d0b-f89598c7261b
policies.displayName: Keys should be backed by a hardware security module (HSM)
policies.description: An HSM is a hardware security module that stores keys. An HSM provides a physical layer of protection for cryptographic keys. The cryptographic key cannot leave a physical HSM which provides a greater level of security than a software key.

policies.name: 75c4f823-d65c-4f29-a733-01d0077fdbcb
policies.displayName: Keys should be the specified cryptographic type RSA or EC
policies.description: Some applications require the use of keys backed by a specific cryptographic type. Enforce a particular cryptographic key type, RSA or EC, in your environment.

policies.name: d8cf8476-a2ec-4916-896e-992351803c44
policies.displayName: Keys should have a rotation policy ensuring that their rotation is scheduled within the specified number of days after creation.
policies.description: Manage your organizational compliance requirements by specifying the maximum number of days after key creation until it must be rotated.

policies.name: 5ff38825-c5d8-47c5-b70e-069a21955146
policies.displayName: Keys should have more than the specified number of days before expiration
policies.description: If a key is too close to expiration, an organizational delay to rotate the key may result in an outage. Keys should be rotated at a specified number of days prior to expiration to provide sufficient time to react to a failure.

policies.name: 49a22571-d204-4c91-a7b6-09b1a586fbc9
policies.displayName: Keys should have the specified maximum validity period
policies.description: Manage your organizational compliance requirements by specifying the maximum amount of time in days that a key can be valid within your key vault.

policies.name: c26e4b24-cf98-4c67-b48b-5a25c4c69eb9
policies.displayName: Keys should not be active for longer than the specified number of days
policies.description: Specify the number of days that a key should be active. Keys that are used for an extended period of time increase the probability that an attacker could compromise the key. As a good security practice, make sure that your keys have not been active longer than two years.

policies.name: 51fb1409-3c36-43c4-a750-ce814ac35ea6
policies.displayName: Keys using AES cryptography should have a specified minimum key size
policies.description: Set the minimum allowed key size for use with your key vaults. Use of AES keys with small key sizes is not a secure practice and doesn't meet many industry certification requirements.

policies.name: ff25f3c8-b739-4538-9d07-3d6d25cfb255
policies.displayName: Keys using elliptic curve cryptography should have the specified curve names
policies.description: Keys backed by elliptic curve cryptography can have different curve names. Some applications are only compatible with specific elliptic curve keys. Enforce the types of elliptic curve keys that are allowed to be created in your environment.

policies.name: 82067dbb-e53b-4e06-b631-546d197452d9
policies.displayName: Keys using RSA cryptography should have a specified minimum key size
policies.description: Set the minimum allowed key size for use with your key vaults. Use of RSA keys with small key sizes is not a secure practice and doesn't meet many industry certification requirements.

policies.name: 1a3b9003-eac6-4d39-a184-4a567ace7645
policies.displayName: Kubernetes cluster container images must include the preStop hook
policies.description: Requires that container images include a preStop hook to gracefully terminate processes during pod shutdowns.

policies.name: 021f8078-41a0-40e6-81b6-c6597da9f3ee
policies.displayName: Kubernetes cluster container images should not include latest image tag
policies.description: Requires that container images do not use the latest tag in Kubernetes, it is a best practice to ensure reproducibility, prevent unintended updates, and facilitate easier debugging and rollbacks by using explicit and versioned container images.

policies.name: e345eecc-fa47-480f-9e88-67dcc122b164
policies.displayName: Kubernetes cluster containers CPU and memory resource limits should not exceed the specified limits
policies.description: Enforce container CPU and memory resource limits to prevent resource exhaustion attacks in a Kubernetes cluster. This policy is generally available for Kubernetes Service (AKS), and preview for Azure Arc enabled Kubernetes. For more information, see https://aka.ms/kubepolicydoc.

policies.name: 03a4ecdb-0684-4039-be91-2762979e1bc8
policies.displayName: Kubernetes cluster containers CPU and memory resource requests must be defined
policies.description: Enforce container CPU and memory resource requests to ensure scheduled node has required resources.

policies.name: 47a1ee2f-2a2a-4576-bf2a-e0e36709c2b8
policies.displayName: Kubernetes cluster containers should not share host namespaces
policies.description: Block pod containers from sharing the host process ID namespace, host IPC namespace, and host network namespace in a Kubernetes cluster. This recommendation aligns with the Kubernetes Pod Security Standards for host namespaces and is part of CIS 5.2.1, 5.2.2 and 5.2.3 which are intended to improve the security of your Kubernetes environments. This policy is generally available for Kubernetes Service (AKS), and preview for Azure Arc enabled Kubernetes. For more information, see https://aka.ms/kubepolicydoc.

policies.name: 56d0a13f-712f-466b-8416-56fb354fb823
policies.displayName: Kubernetes cluster containers should not use forbidden sysctl interfaces
policies.description: Containers should not use forbidden sysctl interfaces in a Kubernetes cluster. This policy is generally available for Kubernetes Service (AKS), and preview for Azure Arc enabled Kubernetes. For more information, see https://aka.ms/kubepolicydoc.

policies.name: 12db3749-7e03-4b9f-b443-d37d3fb9f8d9
policies.displayName: Kubernetes cluster containers should only pull images when image pull secrets are present
policies.description: Restrict containers' image pulls to enforce the presence of ImagePullSecrets, ensuring secure and authorized access to images within a Kubernetes cluster

policies.name: 511f5417-5d12-434d-ab2e-816901e72a5e
policies.displayName: Kubernetes cluster containers should only use allowed AppArmor profiles
policies.description: Containers should only use allowed AppArmor profiles in a Kubernetes cluster. This policy is generally available for Kubernetes Service (AKS), and preview for Azure Arc enabled Kubernetes. For more information, see https://aka.ms/kubepolicydoc.

policies.name: c26596ff-4d70-4e6a-9a30-c2506bd2f80c
policies.displayName: Kubernetes cluster containers should only use allowed capabilities
policies.description: Restrict the capabilities to reduce the attack surface of containers in a Kubernetes cluster. This recommendation is part of CIS 5.2.8 and CIS 5.2.9 which are intended to improve the security of your Kubernetes environments. This policy is generally available for Kubernetes Service (AKS), and preview for Azure Arc enabled Kubernetes. For more information, see https://aka.ms/kubepolicydoc.

policies.name: febd0533-8e55-448f-b837-bd0e06f16469
policies.displayName: Kubernetes cluster containers should only use allowed images
policies.description: Use images from trusted registries to reduce the Kubernetes cluster's exposure risk to unknown vulnerabilities, security issues and malicious images. For more information, see https://aka.ms/kubepolicydoc.

policies.name: f85eb0dd-92ee-40e9-8a76-db25a507d6d3
policies.displayName: Kubernetes cluster containers should only use allowed ProcMountType
policies.description: Pod containers can only use allowed ProcMountTypes in a Kubernetes cluster. This policy is generally available for Kubernetes Service (AKS), and preview for Azure Arc enabled Kubernetes. For more information, see https://aka.ms/kubepolicydoc.

policies.name: 50c83470-d2f0-4dda-a716-1938a4825f62
policies.displayName: Kubernetes cluster containers should only use allowed pull policy
policies.description: Restrict containers' pull policy to enforce containers to use only allowed images on deployments

policies.name: 975ce327-682c-4f2e-aa46-b9598289b86c
policies.displayName: Kubernetes cluster containers should only use allowed seccomp profiles
policies.description: Pod containers can only use allowed seccomp profiles in a Kubernetes cluster. This policy is generally available for Kubernetes Service (AKS), and preview for Azure Arc enabled Kubernetes. For more information, see https://aka.ms/kubepolicydoc.

policies.name: df49d893-a74c-421d-bc95-c663042e5b80
policies.displayName: Kubernetes cluster containers should run with a read only root file system
policies.description: Run containers with a read only root file system to protect from changes at run-time with malicious binaries being added to PATH in a Kubernetes cluster. This policy is generally available for Kubernetes Service (AKS), and preview for Azure Arc enabled Kubernetes. For more information, see https://aka.ms/kubepolicydoc.

policies.name: f4a8fce0-2dd5-4c21-9a36-8f0ec809d663
policies.displayName: Kubernetes cluster pod FlexVolume volumes should only use allowed drivers
policies.description: Pod FlexVolume volumes should only use allowed drivers in a Kubernetes cluster. This policy is generally available for Kubernetes Service (AKS), and preview for Azure Arc enabled Kubernetes. For more information, see https://aka.ms/kubepolicydoc.

policies.name: 098fc59e-46c7-4d99-9b16-64990e543d75
policies.displayName: Kubernetes cluster pod hostPath volumes should only use allowed host paths
policies.description: Limit pod HostPath volume mounts to the allowed host paths in a Kubernetes Cluster. This policy is generally available for Kubernetes Service (AKS), and Azure Arc enabled Kubernetes. For more information, see https://aka.ms/kubepolicydoc.

policies.name: e1e6c427-07d9-46ab-9689-bfa85431e636
policies.displayName: Kubernetes cluster pods and containers should follow SELinux security standards
policies.description: This policy enforces Kubernetes Pod Security Standards for SELinux options. Under PSS mode, 'user' and 'role' fields must be empty, and 'type' field must be one of the allowed values. For more information, see https://aka.ms/kubepolicydoc.

policies.name: f06ddb64-5fa3-4b77-b166-acb36f7f6042
policies.displayName: Kubernetes cluster pods and containers should only run with approved user and group IDs
policies.description: Control the user, primary group, supplemental group and file system group IDs that pods and containers can use to run in a Kubernetes Cluster. This policy is generally available for Kubernetes Service (AKS), and preview for Azure Arc enabled Kubernetes. For more information, see https://aka.ms/kubepolicydoc.

policies.name: 16697877-1118-4fb1-9b65-9898ec2509ec
policies.displayName: Kubernetes cluster pods should only use allowed volume types
policies.description: Pods can only use allowed volume types in a Kubernetes cluster. This policy is generally available for Kubernetes Service (AKS), and preview for Azure Arc enabled Kubernetes. For more information, see https://aka.ms/kubepolicydoc.

policies.name: 82985f06-dc18-4a48-bc1c-b9f4f0098cfe
policies.displayName: Kubernetes cluster pods should only use approved host network and port list
policies.description: Restrict pod access to the host network and the allowable host ports in a Kubernetes cluster. This recommendation is part of CIS 5.2.4 which is intended to improve the security of your Kubernetes environments and aligns with Pod Security Standards (PSS) for hostPorts. This policy is generally available for Kubernetes Service (AKS), and preview for Azure Arc enabled Kubernetes. For more information, see https://aka.ms/kubepolicydoc.

policies.name: 46592696-4c7b-4bf3-9e45-6c2763bdc0a6
policies.displayName: Kubernetes cluster pods should use specified labels
policies.description: Use specified labels to identify the pods in a Kubernetes cluster. This policy is generally available for Kubernetes Service (AKS), and preview for Azure Arc enabled Kubernetes. For more information, see https://aka.ms/kubepolicydoc.

policies.name: 233a2a17-77ca-4fb1-9b6b-69223d272a44
policies.displayName: Kubernetes cluster services should listen only on allowed ports
policies.description: Restrict services to listen only on allowed ports to secure access to the Kubernetes cluster. This policy is generally available for Kubernetes Service (AKS), and preview for Azure Arc enabled Kubernetes. For more information, see https://aka.ms/kubepolicydoc.

policies.name: d46c275d-1680-448d-b2ec-e495a3b6cc89
policies.displayName: Kubernetes cluster services should only use allowed external IPs
policies.description: Use allowed external IPs to avoid the potential attack (CVE-2020-8554) in a Kubernetes cluster. For more information, see https://aka.ms/kubepolicydoc.

policies.name: b0fdedee-7b9e-4a17-9f5d-5e8e912d2f01
policies.displayName: Kubernetes cluster services should use unique selectors
policies.description: Ensure Services in a Namespace Have Unique Selectors. A unique service selector ensures that each service within a namespace is uniquely identifiable based on specific criteria. This policy syncs service resources into OPA via Gatekeeper. Before applying, verify Gatekeeper pods memory capacity won't be exceeded. Parameters apply to specific namespaces, but it syncs all resources of that type across all namespaces. Currently in preview for Kubernetes Service (AKS).

policies.name: 95edb821-ddaf-4404-9732-666045e056b4
policies.displayName: Kubernetes cluster should not allow privileged containers
policies.description: Do not allow privileged containers creation in a Kubernetes cluster. This recommendation is part of CIS 5.2.1 which is intended to improve the security of your Kubernetes environments. This policy is generally available for Kubernetes Service (AKS), and preview for Azure Arc enabled Kubernetes. For more information, see https://aka.ms/kubepolicydoc.

policies.name: 65280eef-c8b4-425e-9aec-af55e55bf581
policies.displayName: Kubernetes cluster should not use naked pods
policies.description: Block usage of naked Pods. Naked Pods will not be rescheduled in the event of a node failure. Pods should be managed by Deployment, Replicset, Daemonset or Jobs

policies.name: a2abc456-f0ae-464b-bd3a-07a3cdbd7fb1
policies.displayName: Kubernetes cluster Windows containers should not overcommit cpu and memory
policies.description: Windows container resource requests should be less or equal to the resource limit or unspecified to avoid overcommit. If Windows memory is over-provisioned it will process pages in disk - which can slow down performance - instead of terminating the container with out-of-memory

policies.name: 5485eac0-7e8f-4964-998b-a44f4f0c1e75
policies.displayName: Kubernetes cluster Windows containers should not run as ContainerAdministrator
policies.description: Prevent usage of ContainerAdministrator as the user to execute the container processes for Windows pods or containers. This recommendation is intended to improve the security of Windows nodes. For more information, see https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/windows/intro/ .

policies.name: 57dde185-5c62-4063-b965-afbb201e9c1c
policies.displayName: Kubernetes cluster Windows containers should only run with approved user and domain user group
policies.description: Control the user that Windows pods and containers can use to run in a Kubernetes Cluster. This recommendation is part of Pod Security Policies on Windows nodes which are intended to improve the security of your Kubernetes environments.

policies.name: 077f0ce1-86d6-4058-bc60-de05067e8622
policies.displayName: Kubernetes cluster Windows pods should not run HostProcess containers
policies.description: Prevent prviledged access to the windows node. This recommendation is intended to improve the security of Windows nodes. For more information, see https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/windows/intro/ .

policies.name: 1a5b4dca-0b6f-4cf5-907c-56316bc1bf3d
policies.displayName: Kubernetes clusters should be accessible only over HTTPS
policies.description: Use of HTTPS ensures authentication and protects data in transit from network layer eavesdropping attacks. This capability is currently generally available for Kubernetes Service (AKS), and in preview for Azure Arc enabled Kubernetes. For more info, visit https://aka.ms/kubepolicydoc

policies.name: 423dd1ba-798e-40e4-9c4d-b6902674b423
policies.displayName: Kubernetes clusters should disable automounting API credentials
policies.description: Disable automounting API credentials to prevent a potentially compromised Pod resource to run API commands against Kubernetes clusters. For more information, see https://aka.ms/kubepolicydoc.

policies.name: a3dc4946-dba6-43e6-950d-f96532848c9f
policies.displayName: Kubernetes clusters should ensure that the cluster-admin role is only used where required
policies.description: The role 'cluster-admin' provides wide-ranging powers over the environment and should be used only where and when needed.

policies.name: ca8d5704-aa2b-40cf-b110-dc19052825ad
policies.displayName: Kubernetes clusters should minimize wildcard use in role and cluster role
policies.description: Using wildcards '*' can be a security risk because it grants broad permissions that may not be necessary for a specific role. If a role has too many permissions, it could potentially be abused by an attacker or compromised user to gain unauthorized access to resources in the cluster.

policies.name: 1c6e92c9-99f0-4e55-9cf2-0c234dc48f99
policies.displayName: Kubernetes clusters should not allow container privilege escalation
policies.description: Do not allow containers to run with privilege escalation to root in a Kubernetes cluster. This recommendation is part of CIS 5.2.5 which is intended to improve the security of your Kubernetes environments. This policy is generally available for Kubernetes Service (AKS), and preview for Azure Arc enabled Kubernetes. For more information, see https://aka.ms/kubepolicydoc.

policies.name: 1ddac26b-ed48-4c30-8cc5-3a68c79b8001
policies.displayName: Kubernetes clusters should not allow endpoint edit permissions of ClusterRole/system:aggregate-to-edit
policies.description: ClusterRole/system:aggregate-to-edit should not allow endpoint edit permissions due to CVE-2021-25740, Endpoint & EndpointSlice permissions allow cross-Namespace forwarding, https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/103675. This policy is generally available for Kubernetes Service (AKS), and preview for Azure Arc enabled Kubernetes. For more information, see https://aka.ms/kubepolicydoc.

policies.name: d2e7ea85-6b44-4317-a0be-1b951587f626
policies.displayName: Kubernetes clusters should not grant CAP_SYS_ADMIN security capabilities
policies.description: To reduce the attack surface of your containers, restrict CAP_SYS_ADMIN Linux capabilities. For more information, see https://aka.ms/kubepolicydoc.

policies.name: a27c700f-8a22-44ec-961c-41625264370b
policies.displayName: Kubernetes clusters should not use specific security capabilities
policies.description: Prevent specific security capabilities in Kubernetes clusters to prevent ungranted privileges on the Pod resource. For more information, see https://aka.ms/kubepolicydoc.

policies.name: 9f061a12-e40d-4183-a00e-171812443373
policies.displayName: Kubernetes clusters should not use the default namespace
policies.description: Prevent usage of the default namespace in Kubernetes clusters to protect against unauthorized access for ConfigMap, Pod, Secret, Service, and ServiceAccount resource types. For more information, see https://aka.ms/kubepolicydoc.

policies.name: d8c942c6-16a3-400b-8f2e-785f44030036
policies.displayName: Kubernetes clusters should specify host in ingress resource rules
policies.description: Ensure specifying host in ingress resource rules to prevent unintentional exposure of backend services to unauthorized access. This policy evaluates Kubernetes Ingress resources to ensure that each rule has a specified host field.

policies.name: 4f3823b6-6dac-4b5a-9c61-ce1afb829f17
policies.displayName: Kubernetes clusters should use Container Storage Interface(CSI) driver StorageClass
policies.description: The Container Storage Interface (CSI) is a standard for exposing arbitrary block and file storage systems to containerized workloads on Kubernetes. In-tree provisioner StorageClass should be deprecated since AKS version 1.21. To learn more, https://aka.ms/aks-csi-driver

policies.name: 3fc4dc25-5baf-40d8-9b05-7fe74c1bc64e
policies.displayName: Kubernetes clusters should use internal load balancers
policies.description: Use internal load balancers to make a Kubernetes service accessible only to applications running in the same virtual network as the Kubernetes cluster. For more information, see https://aka.ms/kubepolicydoc.

policies.name: 9a5f4e39-e427-4d5d-ae73-93db00328bec
policies.displayName: Kubernetes resources should have required annotations
policies.description: Ensure that required annotations are attached on a given Kubernetes resource kind for improved resource management of your Kubernetes resources. This policy is generally available for Kubernetes Service (AKS), and preview for Azure Arc enabled Kubernetes. For more information, see https://aka.ms/kubepolicydoc.

policies.name: fb893a29-21bb-418c-a157-e99480ec364c
policies.displayName: Kubernetes Services should be upgraded to a non-vulnerable Kubernetes version
policies.description: Upgrade your Kubernetes service cluster to a later Kubernetes version to protect against known vulnerabilities in your current Kubernetes version. Vulnerability CVE-2019-9946 has been patched in Kubernetes versions 1.11.9+, 1.12.7+, 1.13.5+, and 1.14.0+

policies.name: a6e9cf2d-7d76-440e-b795-8da246bd3aab
policies.displayName: Lab Services should enable all options for auto shutdown
policies.description: This policy provides helps with cost management by enforcing all automatic shutdown options are enabled for a lab.

policies.name: e8a5a3eb-1ab6-4657-a701-7ae432cf14e1
policies.displayName: Lab Services should not allow template virtual machines for labs
policies.description: This policy prevents creation and customization of a template virtual machines for labs managed through Lab Services.

policies.name: 0fd9915e-cab3-4f24-b200-6e20e1aa276a
policies.displayName: Lab Services should require non-admin user for labs
policies.description: This policy requires non-admin user accounts to be created for the labs managed through lab-services.

policies.name: 3e13d504-9083-4912-b935-39a085db2249
policies.displayName: Lab Services should restrict allowed virtual machine SKU sizes
policies.description: This policy enables you to restrict certain Compute VM SKUs for labs managed through Lab Services. This will restrict certain virtual machine sizes.

policies.name: 2af551d5-1775-326a-0589-590bfb7e9eb2
policies.displayName: Limit privileges to make changes in production environment
policies.description: CMA_C1206 - Limit privileges to make changes in production environment

policies.name: f17d891d-ff20-46f2-bad3-9e0a5403a4d3
policies.displayName: Linux Arc-enabled machines should have Azure Monitor Agent installed
policies.description: Linux Arc-enabled machines should be monitored and secured through the deployed Azure Monitor Agent. The Azure Monitor Agent collects telemetry data from the guest OS. This policy will audit Arc-enabled machines in supported regions. Learn more: https://aka.ms/AMAOverview.

policies.name: fc9b3da7-8347-4380-8e70-0a0361d8dedd
policies.displayName: Linux machines should meet requirements for the Azure compute security baseline
policies.description: Requires that prerequisites are deployed to the policy assignment scope. For details, visit https://aka.ms/gcpol. Machines are non-compliant if the machine is not configured correctly for one of the recommendations in the Azure compute security baseline.

policies.name: 73db37c4-f180-4b0f-ab2c-8ee96467686b
policies.displayName: Linux machines should only have local accounts that are allowed
policies.description: Requires that prerequisites are deployed to the policy assignment scope. For details, visit https://aka.ms/gcpol. Managing user accounts using Azure Active Directory is a best practice for management of identities. Reducing local machine accounts helps prevent the proliferation of identities managed outside a central system. Machines are non-compliant if local user accounts exist that are enabled and not listed in the policy parameter.

policies.name: 32ade945-311e-4249-b8a4-a549924234d7
policies.displayName: Linux virtual machine scale sets should have Azure Monitor Agent installed
policies.description: Linux virtual machine scale sets should be monitored and secured through the deployed Azure Monitor Agent. The Azure Monitor Agent collects telemetry data from the guest OS. This policy will audit virtual machine scale sets with supported OS images in supported regions. Learn more: https://aka.ms/AMAOverview.

policies.name: ca88aadc-6e2b-416c-9de2-5a0f01d1693f
policies.displayName: Linux virtual machines should enable Azure Disk Encryption or EncryptionAtHost.
policies.description: Although a virtual machine's OS and data disks are encrypted-at-rest by default using platform managed keys; resource disks (temp disks), data caches, and data flowing between Compute and Storage resources are not encrypted. Use Azure Disk Encryption or EncryptionAtHost to remediate. Visit https://aka.ms/diskencryptioncomparison to compare encryption offerings. This policy requires two prerequisites to be deployed to the policy assignment scope. For details, visit https://aka.ms/gcpol.

policies.name: 1afdc4b6-581a-45fb-b630-f1e6051e3e7a
policies.displayName: Linux virtual machines should have Azure Monitor Agent installed
policies.description: Linux virtual machines should be monitored and secured through the deployed Azure Monitor Agent. The Azure Monitor Agent collects telemetry data from the guest OS. This policy will audit virtual machines with supported OS images in supported regions. Learn more: https://aka.ms/AMAOverview.

policies.name: a3be3bae-0be0-4903-a924-edb7375c1d2e
policies.displayName: Linux Workloads should comply with the Official CIS Security Benchmark
policies.description: This policy provides you the ability to customize and deploy CIS Security Benchmarks for audit purposes to your Linux workloads across Azure, on-premises and hybrid environments. The contents of the CIS Security Benchmarks are in parity with the benchmarks published at https://cisecurity.org. The policy is powered by azure-osconfig. Requires that prerequisites are deployed to the policy assignment scope. For details, visit https://aka.ms/gcpol.

policies.name: fad40cac-a972-4db0-b204-f1b15cced89a
policies.displayName: Local authentication methods should be disabled on Linux machines
policies.description: Requires that prerequisites are deployed to the policy assignment scope. For details, visit https://aka.ms/gcpol. Machines are non-compliant if Linux servers don't have local authentication methods disabled. This is to validate that Linux Servers can only be accessed by AAD (Azure Active Directory) account or a list of explicitly allowed users by this policy, improving overall security posture.

policies.name: 5fe81c49-16b6-4870-9cee-45d13bf902ce
policies.displayName: Local authentication methods should be disabled on Windows Servers
policies.description: Requires that prerequisites are deployed to the policy assignment scope. For details, visit https://aka.ms/gcpol. Machines are non-compliant if Windows servers don't have local authentication methods disabled. This is to validate that Windows Servers can only be accessed by AAD (Azure Active Directory) account or a list of explicitly allowed users by this policy, improving overall security posture.

policies.name: 15fdbc87-8a47-4ee9-a2aa-9a2ea1f37554
policies.displayName: Log Analytics agent should be installed on your Cloud Services (extended support) role instances
policies.description: Security Center collects data from your Cloud Services (extended support) role instances to monitor for security vulnerabilities and threats.

policies.name: 6c53d030-cc64-46f0-906d-2bc061cd1334
policies.displayName: Log Analytics workspaces should block log ingestion and querying from public networks
policies.description: Improve workspace security by blocking log ingestion and querying from public networks. Only private-link connected networks will be able to ingest and query logs on this workspace. Learn more at https://aka.ms/AzMonPrivateLink#configure-log-analytics.

policies.name: e15effd4-2278-4c65-a0da-4d6f6d1890e2
policies.displayName: Log Analytics Workspaces should block non-Azure Active Directory based ingestion.
policies.description: Enforcing log ingestion to require Azure Active Directory authentication prevents unauthenticated logs from an attacker which could lead to incorrect status, false alerts, and incorrect logs stored in the system.

policies.name: eb6f77b9-bd53-4e35-a23d-7f65d5f0e43d
policies.displayName: Log checkpoints should be enabled for PostgreSQL database servers
policies.description: This policy helps audit any PostgreSQL databases in your environment without log_checkpoints setting enabled.

policies.name: 70be9e12-c935-49ac-9bd8-fd64b85c1f87
policies.displayName: Log checkpoints should be enabled for PostgreSQL flexible servers
policies.description: This policy helps audit any PostgreSQL flexible servers in your environment without log_checkpoints setting enabled.

policies.name: eb6f77b9-bd53-4e35-a23d-7f65d5f0e442
policies.displayName: Log connections should be enabled for PostgreSQL database servers
policies.description: This policy helps audit any PostgreSQL databases in your environment without log_connections setting enabled.

policies.name: 086709ac-11b5-478d-a893-9567a16d2ae3
policies.displayName: Log connections should be enabled for PostgreSQL flexible servers
policies.description: This policy helps audit any PostgreSQL flexible servers in your environment without log_connections setting enabled.

policies.name: eb6f77b9-bd53-4e35-a23d-7f65d5f0e8f3
policies.displayName: Log duration should be enabled for PostgreSQL database servers
policies.description: This policy helps audit any PostgreSQL databases in your environment without log_duration setting enabled.

policies.name: 1fafeaf6-7927-4059-a50a-8eb2a7a6f2b5
policies.displayName: Logic Apps Integration Service Environment should be encrypted with customer-managed keys
policies.description: Deploy into Integration Service Environment to manage encryption at rest of Logic Apps data using customer-managed keys. By default, customer data is encrypted with service-managed keys, but customer-managed keys are commonly required to meet regulatory compliance standards. Customer-managed keys enable the data to be encrypted with an Azure Key Vault key created and owned by you. You have full control and responsibility for the key lifecycle, including rotation and management.

policies.name: dc595cb1-1cde-45f6-8faf-f88874e1c0e1
policies.displayName: Logic Apps should be deployed into Integration Service Environment
policies.description: Deploying Logic Apps into Integration Service Environment in a virtual network unlocks advanced Logic Apps networking and security features and provides you with greater control over your network configuration. Learn more at: https://aka.ms/integration-service-environment. Deploying into Integration Service Environment also allows encryption with customer-managed keys which provides enhanced data protection by allowing you to manage your encryption keys. This is often to meet compliance requirements.

policies.name: d38fc420-0735-4ef3-ac11-c806f651a570
policies.displayName: Long-term geo-redundant backup should be enabled for Azure SQL Databases
policies.description: This policy audits any Azure SQL Database with long-term geo-redundant backup not enabled.

policies.name: bd876905-5b84-4f73-ab2d-2e7a7c4568d9
policies.displayName: Machines should be configured to periodically check for missing system updates
policies.description: To ensure periodic assessments for missing system updates are triggered automatically every 24 hours, the AssessmentMode property should be set to 'AutomaticByPlatform'. Learn more about AssessmentMode property for Windows: https://aka.ms/computevm-windowspatchassessmentmode, for Linux: https://aka.ms/computevm-linuxpatchassessmentmode.

policies.name: 3ac7c827-eea2-4bde-acc7-9568cd320efa
policies.displayName: Machines should have secret findings resolved
policies.description: Audits virtual machines to detect whether they contain secret findings from the secret scanning solutions on your virtual machines.

policies.displayName: Manage transfers between standby and active system components
policies.description: CMA_0371 - Manage transfers between standby and active system components

policies.name: 59953f11-df7f-48b1-870f-1780ed07348e
policies.displayName: Managed Disks and Images should use customer-managed keys for encryption at rest
policies.description: This policy applies exclusively to Mission Platform products and services; usage outside of these scopes is not supported. Use customer-managed keys to manage the encryption at rest of the contents of your managed disks and images. By default, the data is encrypted at rest with platform-managed keys, but customer-managed keys are commonly required to meet regulatory compliance standards.

policies.name: ca91455f-eace-4f96-be59-e6e2c35b4816
policies.displayName: Managed disks should be double encrypted with both platform-managed and customer-managed keys
policies.description: High security sensitive customers who are concerned of the risk associated with any particular encryption algorithm, implementation, or key being compromised can opt for additional layer of encryption using a different encryption algorithm/mode at the infrastructure layer using platform managed encryption keys. The disk encryption sets are required to use double encryption. Learn more at https://aka.ms/disks-doubleEncryption.

policies.name: 8405fdab-1faf-48aa-b702-999c9c172094
policies.displayName: Managed disks should disable public network access
policies.description: Disabling public network access improves security by ensuring that a managed disk isn't exposed on the public internet. Creating private endpoints can limit exposure of managed disks. Learn more at: https://aka.ms/disksprivatelinksdoc.

policies.name: d461a302-a187-421a-89ac-84acdb4edc04
policies.displayName: Managed disks should use a specific set of disk encryption sets for the customer-managed key encryption
policies.description: Requiring a specific set of disk encryption sets to be used with managed disks give you control over the keys used for encryption at rest. You are able to select the allowed encrypted sets and all others are rejected when attached to a disk. Learn more at https://aka.ms/disks-cmk.

policies.name: b874ab2d-72dd-47f1-8cb5-4a306478a4e7
policies.displayName: Managed Identity should be enabled for Container Apps
policies.description: Enforcing managed identity ensures Container Apps can securely authenticate to any resource that supports Azure AD authentication

policies.name: 2d9dbfa3-927b-4cf0-9d0f-08747f971650
policies.displayName: Managed workspace virtual network on Azure Synapse workspaces should be enabled
policies.description: Enabling a managed workspace virtual network ensures that your workspace is network isolated from other workspaces. Data integration and Spark resources deployed in this virtual network also provides user level isolation for Spark activities.

policies.name: b0f33259-77d7-4c9e-aac6-3aabcfae693c
policies.displayName: Management ports of virtual machines should be protected with just-in-time network access control
policies.description: Possible network Just In Time (JIT) access will be monitored by Azure Security Center as recommendations

policies.name: 22730e10-96f6-4aac-ad84-9383d35b5917
policies.displayName: Management ports should be closed on your virtual machines
policies.description: Open remote management ports are exposing your VM to a high level of risk from Internet-based attacks. These attacks attempt to brute force credentials to gain admin access to the machine.

policies.name: 4012c2b7-4e0e-a7ab-1688-4aab43f14420
policies.displayName: Map authenticated identities to individuals
policies.description: CMA_0372 - Map authenticated identities to individuals

policies.name: c707daa0-b93b-454d-9e1e-8ac59866316c
policies.displayName: Maps account should not process data globally.
policies.description: This policy restricts the data processing locations you can add to your Azure Maps accounts. Use to enforce your geo-compliance requirements.

policies.name: dfbd9a64-6114-48de-a47d-90574dc2e489
policies.displayName: MariaDB server should use a virtual network service endpoint
policies.description: Virtual network based firewall rules are used to enable traffic from a specific subnet to Azure Database for MariaDB while ensuring the traffic stays within the Azure boundary. This policy provides a way to audit if the Azure Database for MariaDB has virtual network service endpoint being used.

policies.name: dad1887d-161b-7b61-2e4d-5124a7b5724e
policies.displayName: Measure the time between flaw identification and flaw remediation
policies.description: CMA_C1674 - Measure the time between flaw identification and flaw remediation

policies.name: c43e4a30-77cb-48ab-a4dd-93f175c63b57
policies.displayName: Microsoft Antimalware for Azure should be configured to automatically update protection signatures
policies.description: This policy audits any Windows virtual machine not configured with automatic update of Microsoft Antimalware protection signatures.

policies.name: 1f90fc71-a595-4066-8974-d4d0802e8ef0
policies.displayName: Microsoft Defender CSPM should be enabled
policies.description: Defender Cloud Security Posture Management (CSPM) provides enhanced posture capabilities and a new intelligent cloud security graph to help identify, prioritize, and reduce risk. Defender CSPM is available in addition to the free foundational security posture capabilities turned on by default in Defender for Cloud.

policies.name: c2c0c6d8-007b-4a48-8d9b-3539bddd8e87
policies.displayName: Microsoft Defender for AI Services should be enabled

policies.displayName: Microsoft Defender for APIs should be enabled
policies.description: Microsoft Defender for APIs brings new discovery, protection, detection, & response coverage to monitor for common API based attacks & security misconfigurations.

policies.name: adbe85b5-83e6-4350-ab58-bf3a4f736e5e
policies.displayName: Microsoft Defender for Azure Cosmos DB should be enabled
policies.description:
Microsoft Defender for Azure Cosmos DB is an Azure-native layer of security that detects attempts to exploit databases in your Azure Cosmos DB accounts.
Defender for Azure Cosmos DB detects potential SQL injections, known bad actors based on Microsoft Threat Intelligence, suspicious access patterns, and potential exploitations of your database through compromised identities or malicious insiders.

policies.name: 1c988dd6-ade4-430f-a608-2a3e5b0a6d38
policies.displayName: Microsoft Defender for Containers should be enabled

policies.name: d31e5c31-63b2-4f12-887b-e49456834fa1
policies.displayName: Microsoft Defender for SQL should be enabled for unprotected Synapse workspaces
policies.description: Enable Defender for SQL to protect your Synapse workspaces. Defender for SQL monitors your Synapse SQL to detect anomalous activities indicating unusual and potentially harmful attempts to access or exploit databases.

policies.name: 640d2586-54d2-465f-877f-9ffc1d2109f4
policies.displayName: Microsoft Defender for Storage should be enabled
policies.description: Microsoft Defender for Storage detects potential threats to your storage accounts. It helps prevent the three major impacts on your data and workload: malicious file uploads, sensitive data exfiltration, and data corruption. The new Defender for Storage plan includes Malware Scanning and Sensitive Data Threat Detection. This plan also provides a predictable pricing structure (per storage account) for control over coverage and costs.

policies.name: 882e19a6-996f-400e-a30f-c090887254f4
policies.displayName: Migrate WAF from WAF Config to WAF Policy on Application Gateway
policies.description: If you have WAF Config instead of WAF Policy, then you may want to move to the new WAF Policy. Going forward, the firewall policy will support WAF policy settings, managed rulesets, exclusions, and disabled rule-groups.

policies.displayName: Modify - Configure Azure Event Grid domains to disable public network access
policies.description: Disable public network access for Azure Event Grid resource so that it isn't accessible over the public internet. This will help protect them against data leakage risks.
